Correction to the mapper: the daemon does NOT run launcher.list_sessions (no launcher import in monitor_daemon.py; it uses session_manager.list_sessions at :1111). BUT the daemon's own loop flips the same session: status_detector_dispatcher.py:254 returns (STATUS_TERMINATED, 'Window no longer exists', '') for a missing window, and monitor_daemon.py:1447-1450 persists 'terminated' whenever `session.status != 'terminated' and not pane_content` (every 2 s loop, INTERVAL_FAST settings.py:156). verdict.reason: Verified in textual 7.5.0 (the venv's version): worker_manager.WorkerManager.add_worker -> `if exclusive and worker.group: self.cancel_group(...)`; cancel_group -> Worker.cancel() which only sets `_cancelled`, calls `self._task.cancel()` and sets `cancelled_event` (no join); Worker._run_threaded ends in `await loop.run_in_executor(None, runner, self._work)` — asyncio's default ThreadPoolExecutor (max_workers=min(32, cpu+4) = 20 on this 16-core box; grep found no set_default_executor/ThreadPoolExecutor in textual/app.py or worker.py). Cancelling the task raises CancelledError at the await; a pending (not yet started) concurrent future is cancelled by asyncio's future chaining, but a RUNNING thread body is never interrupted. Empirical proof (scratchpad/bench_l5_02.py, headless App.run_test): starting an exclusive group='g' thread worker every 0.1 s with a 1 s body -> started=10, max_concurrent_bodies=10, finished=4 at the check point, all 10 eventually finished. verdict.cost_at_reference: Amplifier for L5-01 and L5-04: with a 30 s daemon_status body on a 1 s timer, 20 concurrent transcript scans run in the default executor (all GIL-bound -> process at 100-110% CPU, not 20 cores); the fast_status body is submitted to the same executor via run_in_executor(None) and waits behind them while `_status_update_in_progress` stays True, so the 250 ms status path stops entirely until the executor drains (multi-second to minute-scale UI freezes). sites.operation: Lock hold time per RMW = parse + dump(indent=2) + fsync = 3.8 ms @50 entries, 37 ms @500, 149 ms @2000. The daemon's ~100 RMW per loop therefore hold EX ~19% of wall time at a 50-entry file, ~100% at >=500 entries; each TUI 250 ms tick, each web request and each sister TUI (M_MULTI - all overcode tmux sessions share the ONE ~/.overcode/sessions/sessions.json regardless of tmux session name, session_manager.py:414-417) queues behind it. Additionally every RMW takes a temp-free in-place truncate+rewrite, so a reader without the lock (Windows path) would see partial JSON; on POSIX the retry loops (:429-447, :559-583) sleep 0.1 s x 5 on decode/IO errors.
sites.complexity: writer duty cycle = (2 N_AGENTS RMW per loop x hold time) / 2 s; reader latency ~ duty x hold time
sites.current_bound: none; hold time scales with file size, hold count with N_AGENTS

sites.cadence: every keystroke typed in the bottom pane and every byte of output from the focused agent
sites.operation: keystroke: outer client -> server (overcode pane) -> nested client process -> server (agent pane pty) -> agent; echo: agent -> server render for nested client -> nested client stdout = outer pane pty -> server parses as pane output -> outer client render. Each keystroke and each output frame crosses the single-threaded server twice and is rendered twice (364x52 grid twice). A grouped session also means every window in the group is a candidate for redraw on both clients
sites.complexity: 2x server passes per keystroke and per output frame; echo latency = 2 x (server queue wait + render) ; under fleet load p90 queue wait ~30 ms -> ~60 ms echo
sites.current_bound: structural; bounded per keystroke but multiplies every other site's latency effect on typing

verdict.corrected_complexity: O(1) server passes per keystroke (2 instead of 1); render cost O(V_TERM cells) per pass; independent of N_AGENTS (only the viewed window is rendered).
verdict.fix_preserving_freshness: Remove the second pass instead of slowing anything: on focus change, move the focused agent's real pane into the overcode window with join-pane -s agents:<win> -t overcode:overcode-tmux (and break-pane/move-pane it back on blur), or swap-pane, so keystrokes and output cross the server once; keep the linked-session approach only for the 'attach bare' CLI. verdict.reason: Chain confirmed: tui.py:605 set_interval(1, update_daemon_status) -> 630-633 _fetch_daemon_status_async (thread worker, exclusive, group daemon_status) -> 660-676 -> daemon_status_bar.py:77-86 read_agent_status_history(hours=baseline/60+0.1) then calculate_mean_spin_from_history; gated by baseline_minutes>0 (daemon_status_bar.py:78; default 0 at tui.py:269 but persisted from prefs at tui.py:380 so it stays on across restarts). Per 1 Hz call: _filter list-comp over the whole cache (213-217), _incremental_read trims the whole cache whenever the file changed (136-137; the daemon appends every 2 s), and calculate_mean_spin_from_history list-comps all rows with `agent in agent_names` list membership (tui_logic.py:477-481). The parse itself is incremental (bounded), the three O(window) passes are not.
verdict.cost_now: 8 agents, 3 h cache (~45k rows, ~17 MB resident): 1 Hz path ~1 ms filter + ~2 ms spin(30 min) + ~2 ms incremental trim -> ~5 ms/s (0.5%); with a 180-min baseline ~35 ms/s (3.5%).
verdict.cost_at_reference: 50 agents (measured 279k rows, ~106 MB resident at ~380 B/row): baseline 30 min -> 4.7 + 15.2 + 9.6 = ~30 ms/s (3%); baseline 180 min -> 175 + 75 + 10 = ~260 ms/s (26% of a core) in the daemon_status worker. 200 agents (1.1M rows, ~425 MB resident): 30-min baseline 19 + 108 + 41 = ~170 ms/s (17%); 180-min baseline 695 + 551 = ~1.25 s per 1 s tick -> the exclusive worker overruns; Textual 'cancels' the old thread but it keeps running and serialises on StatusHistoryFile._lock, so threads back up without bound. A 24 h timeline multiplies rows and RSS by 8. Note the same 1 Hz worker also runs compute_window_burn (see H-60c), which is far larger.
verdict.cliff_threshold: >10% of a core at roughly 100-150k cached rows with a 180-min baseline (about 20-25 agents at the 2 s daemon tick, 3 h cache); >100 MB RSS at ~50 agents with the 3 h timeline (~12 agents with a 24 h timeline); worker overrun (>1 s) at ~800k-1M rows.

Textual thread workers run on the loop's default executor (textual/worker.py _run_threaded -> loop.run_in_executor(None)); cancel() only cancels the awaiting task, the thread runs to completion, so overrunning workers stack up to the pool size (min(32, cpu+4) = 20 here) then queue -- and that same executor serves the 4 Hz fast_status and 5 s slow_stats workers.
verdict.cost_now: baseline=0 (default): 0. baseline>0 with 5-10 agents owning 5-20 MB of transcripts: measured real-transcript throughput 300-870 MB/s (~3 ms/MB; 8.9 MB/536 lines in 27 ms, 3.3 MB/1617 lines in 11 ms) -> 15-60 ms per second (1.5-6% of a core) plus the 1 Hz status-history CSV read (AUDIT #157).

Owned-file count also grows with every /clear (agent_session_ids accumulate) and with subagent count. This reproduces '110% CPU for 15 hours' exactly, conditional on the user having a baseline window selected (sticky pref).
verdict.cliff_threshold: Sum of live owned transcript bytes >= ~30 MB -> 10% core; >= ~300 MB -> a full core and runaway thread stacking; both well inside reference (T_TRANSCRIPT 200 MB, N_AGENTS 50).
verdict.freshness_needed: The burn/mu figures summarise a 15-180 min window; 1 Hz is fine but even 5 s would not be noticed. Exact totals matter (they feed cost columns).
verdict.fix_preserving_freshness: Keep 1 Hz and exact totals with an incremental per-file reader: cache {path: (offset, mtime_ns, size, deque[(ts, usage)])}; on each call read only bytes appended since offset (truncate/rotate -> reset), evict deque entries older than `since`, sum the deque. Daemon: same parses at 60 s, ~1/12 of the above.

(5) should_scan_git GIT_STATS_EVERY_SWEEPS=3 (tui_logic.py:963-974; tui.py:1557-1580): diff/untracked columns 5 s -> 15 s, once per distinct directory; each scan is `git diff --stat HEAD` + `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` (tui_helpers.py:257-330, timeout 2 s), O(working tree). (6) read_git_context_from_disk in _detect_git_context (session_manager.py:666-690) -- no trade, but refresh_git_context still does a full get_session per agent per tick (718-736) = H-61. (1) hook fast path not re-verified here. Residual scaling is owned by H-61 (sessions.json traffic) and H-66 (captures still linear in N).
verdict.cost_now: (5): 5-10 agents in 1-3 repos -> 2-6 git spawns per 15 s, ~20-100 ms each on a mid-size repo (<1% core). (2): 9-14 captures/s (see H-66).
verdict.cost_at_reference: (5): 50 agents in ~10 distinct repos -> 20 git spawns per 15 s; on a 100k-file repo `ls-files --others` can take 0.3-1 s and hits the 2 s timeout on huge trees -> up to ~10 s CPU per 15 s across the 8-thread pool (a repo-size axis, not in the list). (2)/(6): see H-66 / H-61 for the linear-in-N residuals.
verdict.cliff_threshold: (5): >= ~8 distinct large (>=50k-file) repos, or any repo where the two git commands exceed ~1.5 s (10% core at 15 s cadence). (2),(6): inherit H-66 / H-61 cliffs.
verdict.freshness_needed: diff/untracked counts are informational: 15 s is acceptable; non-focused pane-derived columns: 1-2 s acceptable; branch name: 2-10 s.
verdict.fix_preserving_freshness: (5) one `git status --porcelain=v2 -z --untracked-files=all` per repo gives both counts (halves spawns), and enable/detect core.fsmonitor so untracked walks are cheap; optionally gate on .git/index mtime + top-level dir mtimes. (6) fix H-61 so the subprocess win is not eaten by JSON loads. (2) fix H-66 so non-focused captures are event-gated rather than time-sliced.

sites.function: TUI polls four shared state files by full re-parse; aggregated parse budget
sites.trigger: historical incident docs/architecture.md 'What's Concerning' §4 (daemon coupling via shared files; TUI reads all four) (2026-09-20)
sites.cadence: see incident
sites.operation: The daemon, session manager, status history and presence logger each write a file the TUI re-reads; no schema/versioning, no change gating at read time.
sites.complexity: see incident
sites.current_bound: None at the loader level (history CSV has mtime+incremental cache; presence has mtime cache; sessions.json and monitor_daemon_state.json have none).
sites.cost_at_reference_scale: unknown
sites.cliff: Per second in the TUI: sessions.json ~5.5-6.5 full parses (AUDIT #127 incident); monitor_daemon_state.json ~5-6 full parses -- fast path 4 Hz (tui.py:1386), daemon status 1 Hz (642), daemon_panel 1 Hz when open (daemon_panel.py:52), update_session_widgets every 10 s (2034) -- at ~3 KB/session (measured 9.1 KB / 3 sessions) that is 150 KB at 50 agents (~10 ms/s) and 600 KB at 200 (~40 ms/s) via MonitorDaemonState.load json.load + from_dict (monitor_daemon_state.py:288-307); agent_status_history.csv incremental at 1 Hz + O(window) filtering (AUDIT #157); presence every ~60 s. verdict.reason: No change gate at the loader: SessionManager._load_state is LOCK_SH + json.load every call (session_manager.py:505-540); MonitorDaemonState.load is json.load + from_dict every call (monitor_daemon_state.py:288-307; get_monitor_daemon_state 333-347). The 1 s TTL _get_cached_sessions (tui.py:1109-1125) has ZERO callers -- dead code. sessions.json full parses per second in the TUI: fast path 4 Hz (tui.py:1371, inside _fetch_statuses_async 1364, guarded by _status_update_in_progress), daemon-status 1 Hz (656) plus another 1 Hz at daemon_status_bar.py:99 when baseline>0, stats sweep 0.2 Hz (1546), refresh_sessions 0.1 Hz (897 -> launcher.py:927), summaries 0.2 Hz when enabled (1973): ~5.3-6.5/s. monitor_daemon_state.json: 4 Hz (1386) + 1 Hz (642) + 1 Hz daemon_panel only while displayed (daemon_panel.py:45-52 `if not self.display: return`) + 0.1 Hz (2034): ~5-6/s. sessions.json size follows N_SESSIONS_TOTAL because terminated entries are only removed by CLI `overcode cleanup` (cli/agent.py:156). Presence and history CSV readers are mtime/incremental (AUDIT #157) -- out of this batch.
verdict.cost_now: Measured: sessions.json 22 KB/4 entries ~0.1 ms x 6/s (~0.1%); daemon state 9 KB ~0.1 ms x 6/s. Negligible today -- yet json scanstring topped the 2026-09-20 sample, consistent with the 4 Hz + 1 Hz + 1 Hz parses being the only steady CPU when agents are idle.
verdict.cost_at_reference: sessions.json at 50 live entries (0.40 MB): 0.7 ms parse + ~1 ms from_dict -> ~10 ms/s (1%); at 200 entries / 1.59 MB: list_sessions 7.7 ms -> ~45-50 ms/s (~5%); at 2000 un-cleaned entries (~16 MB): ~80 ms x 6 = ~0.5 s/s (50% of a core). Each read can additionally wait up to ~22 ms behind a daemon LOCK_EX RMW (H-61) at 1.6 MB. monitor_daemon_state.json: 1.0 ms at 50 sessions (128 KB) -> 6 ms/s (0.6%); 4.0 ms at 200 (508 KB) -> ~24 ms/s (2.4%).
verdict.cliff_threshold: sessions.json >= ~450 entries (~3.5 MB) -> 10% of a core from parses alone (N_SESSIONS_TOTAL axis, reachable at 2,000 without cleanup); daemon state only at N_AGENTS >= ~800. >100 ms stalls do not occur (all reads are in worker threads).
verdict.freshness_needed: Fast path needs the session list only to map widgets to Session objects: exact 250 ms freshness is preserved by any (mtime_ns, size, inode)-gated cache because the writer always changes mtime/size. Daemon state is written once per 2 s tick (monitor_daemon_state.py:260-286 atomic rename), so 4-6 parses/s are 8-12x redundant.
verdict.fix_preserving_freshness: (mtime_ns, size, ino)-gated parse cache in SessionManager._load_state (return a fresh deep copy or make callers non-mutating; _locked_state keeps re-reading under LOCK_EX) and in MonitorDaemonState.load; daemon-state parses drop to 0.5/s and sessions.json parses to its write rate -- which is N per tick until H-61 coalesces writes, so fix H-61 first. Delete the dead _get_cached_sessions.
verdict.benchmark_notes: scratchpad/bench_h.py / bench_h2.py: json.loads of a 1.59 MB 200-entry replica 2.8 ms, Session.from_dict x200 4.0 ms, MonitorDaemonState.load 1.0/4.0 ms at 50/200 sessions (replicas cloned from the real state files, written to scratch).
verdict.corrected_complexity: O(sessions.json bytes) x ~6/s + O(daemon-state bytes) x ~6/s, no gating

bounded_ok.why_bounded: Returns immediately when the panel is hidden (self.display False; live prefs daemon_panel_visible=False); when visible it tail-reads at most 100 lines (tail_file_lines max_lines=100, daemon_logging.py:34 max_bytes 256 KB) and then reads only bytes appended since the saved offset, re-tailing after rotation shrink. Also reads monitor_daemon_state.json (9 KB) once per second.
Same pattern: hidden by default, tail of 100 lines then incremental offset reads; tui.log is 60 KB and last written 1 May (fd 6w open but idle).

monitor_daemon.log is renamed to .1 once it passes 20 MB (observed monitor_daemon.log.1 = 20,971,571 B, live log 5.17 MB growing 4.5 MB/day at 27 lines/min), so disk use is capped at ~40 MB per session dir regardless of U_DAEMON. The per-loop INFO line (monitor_daemon.py:1553) is a small append.

10 Hz tick appends a tuple to an in-memory list that is flushed to diagnostics/event_loop_timing.csv every 5 s (so memory holds <=50 entries); the CSV (45.3 MB now, ~28 MB/day) is hard-capped at 100 MB by cap_diagnostics_csv which reads only the last 10% and rewrites it (settings.py cap_diagnostics_csv: 'f.seek(int(size * 0.9))'), i.e. a 10 MB rewrite roughly every 3 days. Per-tick CPU is a datetime.now().isoformat() — negligible in the sample.
Only scheduled when prefs.status_change_logging is true (live: false); same 100 MB cap via cap_diagnostics_csv; status_changes.csv is 94 KB from March.

bounded_ok.function: StatusHistoryFile.read / _full_read / _incremental_read (used by TUI timeline every 30 s and spin-rate every 1 s)
bounded_ok.why_bounded: Binary-seeks to the cutoff timestamp on first read (4 ms for 1 h, 92 ms for 24 h, 174 ms for 168 h on the 22 MB file) then parses only newly appended bytes (repeat calls 0.1-3 ms); cache invalidates on size shrink (rotation). Growth of the underlying file (L0-06) does not make the read cost grow, only the window's row count does (L0-10).
json.load of a single small overwrite-style file (live hook_state_overcode-main.json = 1,173 B; 181 such files exist but only displayed sessions are read); measured 0.03 ms.

Bounded to the last 50 lines and only invoked from detect_status when event=='Stop' and status is waiting (hook_status_detector.py:690-696); measured 0.29 ms on the 633 KB live file. Caveat recorded in L0-05: the window doubles when lines are huge, so it is bounded in lines, not bytes.

bounded_ok.function: read_session_file_stats mtime+size cache (5 s stats path)
bounded_ok.why_bounded: Warm hits cost 5-29 us per file (measured), and the whole 5 s stats tick for 3 sessions is 16-23 ms with 26 cache entries — bounded while (a) files are unchanged and (b) fewer than 512 files are tracked (both caveats are L0-03).

A tick is skipped while the previous fast-path worker is still running, so the 4 Hz path cannot pile up; only the focused agent is captured at 4 Hz (500 lines) and non-focused agents known to a fresh daemon state are rotated (~1 Hz total), verified at tui.py:1391-1405 and confirmed by the observed spawn rate (~4-5 tmux/s for 3 agents; a96ff0f).

bounded_ok.function: _update_stats_async git scan (should_scan_git sweep + dedup by effective_git_directory)
bounded_ok.why_bounded: Git diff/untracked subprocesses run only on selected sweeps and once per unique directory (tui.py:1560-1577); one git child observed in 20 s. Cost per call vs repository size was not assessed.
Throttled to one request per 300 s (_min_interval) with a 10 s timeout, invoked from the 1 Hz daemon-status worker only when a subscription-metered backend is present.

~/.overcode/jobs is 72 KB / 18 files here; the timer runs on the main thread and its call_from_thread is wrapped in a bare except (tui.py:2751-2752), so its cost is one small state read per 5 s. Job-state file size vs J_JOBS was not measured.

RSS 157,056 KB at start of audit and 157,088 KB 25 minutes later at 19.5 h uptime (peak physical footprint 123.9 MB per sample); daemon RSS 98,272 KB unchanged. No leak visible at this scale/window; 7-day growth not assessable from this run. In-memory caches inspected: _pane_content_cache/_previous_statuses are pruned to displayed sessions (tui.py:1440-1442), _heartbeat_log flushed every 5 s, _session_stats_cache capped at 512.

25 threads (21 idle Textual/asyncio executor workers in SimpleQueue.get, 1 waitpid on the daemon child, 1 log writer, 1 selector) and 39 fds; only one regular file open (tui.log). Daemon: 3 threads (main, presence logger sleeping 60 s, one idle workqueue thread), 34 fds, regular files open: monitor_daemon.lock and presence_log.csv (append). No descriptor growth observed.

Pure O(N) loop over session ids per tick; chooses focused + 1-in-4 rotation (NON_FOCUSED_CAPTURE_EVERY=4, :920) + any id not in daemon_known_ids. Bounded in itself; the unbounded behaviour is the caller passing an empty daemon_known_ids when the daemon is stale (see L1-03 cliff A).

Only does `list(self.query(SessionSummary))` (O(N) DOM walk, ~tens of us at N=50) and starts the worker; the `_status_update_in_progress` flag (:1338, cleared in finally :1526) guarantees at most one fast_status worker at a time, so slow ticks are dropped rather than queued (self-throttling, latency degrades instead of piling up).
max_workers=min(8, N): at most 8 OS threads created and joined per tick (32 thread spawns/s, ~0.5 ms/tick overhead); a persistent pool would save that but it does not scale with any axis.

bounded_ok.function: _get_focused_widget / _get_widgets_in_session_order (called ~4x per tick incl. once from the worker thread)
bounded_ok.why_bounded: O(N log N) sort of widget list per call; ~4 calls per tick; at N=200 that is ~4 x 50 us. Note: called from the worker thread at :1379 while the main thread may mutate the DOM — a thread-safety hazard, not a scaling one.
Three query_one lookups plus one CSS query `.modal.visible`; O(DOM size) which is O(N) widgets; microseconds at reference scale.

Guarded by `_column_widths_dirty` (:1000-1001); the flag is set only every 5 s by _apply_stats_results (:1923), every 10 s by update_session_widgets (:2180/:2256) and on column-config changes, so the O(N x 49 columns) recomputation runs ~0.3x/s, not 4x/s.

bounded_ok.function: _apply_status_results daemon enrichment loop (:1467-1489) and subtree_costs extraction (:1492-1500)
bounded_ok.why_bounded: Builds daemon_by_id dict once (O(N)) then O(1) per widget; subtree_costs loop O(N daemon sessions) + O(|_remote_sessions|); trivial per tick.

bounded_ok.function: PollingStatusDetector.detect_status (CPU part, excluding the tmux subprocess)

Each strip_ansi's the capture (O(bytes)) and inspects only the last 40 / 12 lines or scans lines bottom-up until the status bar; measured 0.49 ms total on the 56 KB capture. (Redundant: strip_ansi is executed 3x on the same content; a shared clean copy would cut it ~3x, still bounded.)
Pure functions over the small hook_state dict (pending_obligations list, a handful of keys); O(|obligations|) per capture, obligations are removed on PostToolUse/Stop (hook_handler.py:146-224).

Module-level cache _PATTERNS_BY_BACKEND (:418-420): dict hit after first call per backend; no per-call regex compilation.

Opt-in (status_change_logging pref); buffer swapped every 5 s; rows only on status transitions and focus switches; file capped at 100 MB via cap_diagnostics_csv (:4302). On this machine status_changes.csv is 94 KB.
One Path.touch() per keypress (settings.py:523-537) and one small write_text at most every 5 s (:4091-4093); per-keypress, not per-tick.

Pure O(1) functions over a few strings and set membership tests; called once per widget per tick.

One stat() per call; the 10% tail rewrite only happens once per ~100 MB of growth (~1.3 days at the heartbeat's 70 MB/day) — verified as the bound on both diagnostics CSVs, with the caveat noted in L1-11 that the rewrite runs on the main thread.

bounded_ok.why_bounded: O(|_summaries|) tuple construction per tick; _summaries is keyed by session id and only grows with sessions the summariser has processed (bounded by N_SESSIONS_TOTAL over U_TUI, see L1-13 for the pruning note); a few ms/s at 2,000 entries.
exists() + open + non-blocking flock + close on a 0-byte lock file; O(1) per second, no data growth.

Re-exported pid-file liveness check (same pattern as pid_utils.is_process_running :40-49); O(1).

one fromisoformat; O(1).

One StatusHistoryFile per distinct path; the TUI uses one path (get_agent_history_path(tmux_session)), so the dict holds 1 entry.

One reader per backend name (<=5 entries), memoised.
getattr + at most one os.path.isdir per session per sweep.

O(N_AGENTS) dict lookups per 15 s.

O(fields) per entry (dataclasses.fields + dict filtering); linear in N_SESSIONS_TOTAL, its cost is accounted under L2-01/L2-15.

Only for children that transitioned to done this call; idempotent.

max over N_AGENTS names + one shutil.get_terminal_size ioctl per access; a few accesses per render.

bounded_ok.why_bounded: API calls limited to interval (5 s) / context_interval (15 s) per session and skipped when pane hash unchanged; dicts keyed by session id grow only with distinct sessions seen during the TUI's life (<= N_SESSIONS_TOTAL, small values).

_pending only receives an entry when should_send_stall_notification is true (tui.py:1811-1822, gated by _notified_stalls so once per stall); flush() runs every 250 ms (tui.py:1881) and clears the list except during the 2 s coalesce window (notifier.py:45-64); notification subprocesses are fire-and-forget Popen (notifier.py:15-19) and Python's subprocess module reaps abandoned Popen objects, so no zombie accumulation. Steady state is 2 subprocess spawns per 15 s (display-message + one list-windows with sizes, tui.py:824-868); resize-window is only sent for windows whose size differs (windows_needing_resize, :869-877), so O(N_AGENTS) spawns happen only right after a real terminal resize. Exclusive group agent_resize.
Purely user-action driven (key presses on remote agents); one HTTP request with a 10 s (or 3 s) timeout per action; no state retained.
One HTTP GET (3 s timeout) plus two linear scans over the S_SISTERS list; response is one agent (100-line pane). Invoked only for the focused remote agent every 1.5 s (L3-08).
O(S_SISTERS + N_remote) list/set comprehension and a single dict-based O(N) pass (name_to_session dict, :1030); no quadratic loops; runs only per refresh_sessions (10 s).

Single-agent HTTP; linear scans over _remote_sessions and the widget query with early break; _remote_sessions is replaced wholesale each poll (tui.py:1648) so it never grows beyond the current remote agent count.

get_summarizer_config resolves 5 config keys through load_config, which has a 5 s TTL plus mtime cache (config.py:21-24, 52-69); called at most once per summarizer toggle/tick, so no per-tick YAML parse.

bounded_ok.function: on_key (signal_activity touch + throttled write_tui_heartbeat + summarizer resume)
bounded_ok.why_bounded: signal_activity performs one Path.touch() per keypress (settings.py:523-537) and write_tui_heartbeat is throttled to once per 5 s (tui.py:4091-4094); both scale only with human keystroke rate. Summarizer resume creates a client once and kicks a single tick.

O(J_JOBS) widget diff per 5 s: dict of existing widgets, remove missing, refresh/mount the rest (tui.py:2764-2786); with show_terminated the list includes every completed job still in jobs.json (see L3-10 for the retention issue), but per-widget cost is a single render.

Single json.load/dump of jobs.json with retries (5 x 0.1 s) — cost is O(J_total) per call and only grows through the missing retention sweep noted in L3-10; no in-memory accumulation (fresh dict per call).

One DOM query + O(N log N) sort (_get_widgets_in_session_order tui.py:2332-2345), a linear scan over S_SISTERS for the stale banner (:2990-3007), and one PreviewPane render of the focused widget's content — O(N_AGENTS log N + V_TERM) per call, bounded by N_AGENTS; called at 4 Hz from the fast path and 1.5 s from L3-08.

Entries keyed by (session, window) with a 30 s TTL (implementations.py:30, 55-60, 92-106); never evicted but each entry is a small libtmux object, so growth is bounded by distinct windows seen (N_SESSIONS_TOTAL x ~200 B). None results are not cached, which is the per-terminated-session spawn noted in L3-02.

bounded_ok.function: summarizer cost cap / idle auto-pause gates
bounded_ok.why_bounded: Verified: summarizer is disabled at construction (tui.py:401-404), pauses after 300 s without keypress (tui.py:1940-1953), and hard-halts at total_cost_usd >= cost_cap (tui.py:1957-1970, default $100). Therefore the summarizer cannot be the cause of a 15-hour unattended 110% CPU burn — it stops itself within 5 minutes of the user walking away. It is still a severe cliff while the user is present with many agents (L3-02..L3-04).

Dict entries are popped when the timer fires, when the agent is visited, or when the bell clears (tui.py:2292, 2306, 1829-1831); at most one key per focused stalled agent. Outstanding Timer tasks are capped at ~20 (5 s window at 4 Hz) — see L3-12 for the redundant writes.

Pure in-memory; ~4 passes over monitor_state.sessions plus a sort in calculate_safe_break_duration (tui_helpers.py:701-758) and a loop over sister sessions; measured 33 us at 50 sessions; O(N_AGENTS + sister sessions) at 1 Hz.

is_supervisor_daemon_running/is_web_server_running are one PID-file read + kill(0) each (pid_utils.py:40-49); SummarizerClient.is_available -> get_summarizer_config uses the config.py cache (5 s TTL + mtime check, config.py:21-71); get_web_server_url reads a tiny port file. Constant ~5 syscalls per second, no growth axis. (The baseline>0 branches are L4-09/L4-10/L4-11.)

Gated by self.display (hidden by default, daemon_panel.py:44-46). First read and post-rotation read use tail_file_lines capped at 256 KB / 100 lines (daemon_logging.py:34-58); steady state reads only bytes appended since the saved offset (bounded by the daemon's write rate); rotation detected via st_size < offset; log_lines capped at 100; render scans <=16 lines with 6 substring tests each. get_monitor_daemon_state per second is a 9 KB JSON parse (96 us measured, O(N_AGENTS)).

Same structure as DaemonPanel: display gate (tui_log_panel.py:65), tail_file_lines 256 KB cap, incremental offset reads, 100-line buffer, <=20 rendered lines with line[:160] truncation. The TUI log is written by the TUI itself so its growth rate is self-limited.
Seeks to size-max_bytes (256 KB) before reading; measured 276 us on a 5.2 MB log; independent of log size (W_WALLCLOCK).
max(len(name)) over sessions (O(N_AGENTS)) and one shutil.get_terminal_size (1.2 us), called twice per render; width clamped to [20, 200].
Dead code in the TUI path (render uses build_timeline_slots); O(rows) if ever called.
Event-driven (user presses f): one Text.from_ansi pass over <=capture_lines (13-26 ms for 500-1,000 lines), hide() does one linear query over SessionSummary widgets. No timer.

Constant work per job (2 fromisoformat, 7 appends, ~30 us). _apply_jobs (tui.py:2783-2787) refreshes every job widget every 5 s unconditionally, but J_JOBS=50 -> 10 renders/s ~ 0.3 ms/s. pane_content reactive compares lists O(lines) once per second only in jobs mode.
All event-driven; _find_target_session is one O(N_AGENTS) in-memory scan; no timers, no file I/O (except L4-14).

Textual reactives fire watchers only when the value changes; the app assigns them on user actions (tui_actions/view.py:135,163) and at widget mount (tui.py:2211-2213), so periodic assignments of equal values do not trigger refresh.

Pure in-memory: 2 fromisoformat, one regex only when busy_sleeping (extract_sleep_duration), function-local imports (sys.modules hits), frozenset class checks; measured 6.2 us. Per-row cost is part of L4-01 but has no independent growth axis.

get_patterns memoizes per backend name in _PATTERNS_BY_BACKEND (status_patterns.py:418-431); get_backend is a dict lookup (backends/__init__.py:46-48).
Not called by the running TUI (grep: no callers of widget.update_status()/apply_status( in tui.py or tui_actions); only the batched apply_status_no_refresh path is live.

Fixed 49-column table (SUMMARY_COLUMNS); per row O(49) with cell_len (Rich LRU-cached for short strings); measured 70 us + 23 us; no growth axis beyond N_AGENTS rows (accounted in L4-01/L4-05). Placeholder/visibility lambdas are O(1).

Per-row micro-allocations: dict copy+update of ~10 entries, settings.get_user_config() is a process-global cache (settings.py:464-469, only reload_user_config re-reads), model_short_name is a dict lookup + small heuristic. All O(1); included in the 110 us row render.
Static tables; get_default_columns_for_level is O(49) and only called from the config modal.

Pure O(1) Text builders; only render_ai_summarizer_section is used at runtime (daemon_status_bar.py:276-298); render_session_summary_line/render_spin_stats/etc. have no runtime callers (test-only legacy).

No transitions/animations declared; :hover/:focus rules trigger repaints only on mouse/focus events; the max-height rules bound the number of painted rows (though not the timeline's render() work, see L4-06).

~8 O(N_AGENTS) passes every 10 s; DOM moves skipped when order already matches (tui.py:2371-2377); widget count = displayed sessions only (filter_visible_sessions) plus terminated ghosts GC'd after 600 s (_TERMINATED_GC_SECONDS tui.py:393, 1884-1895). Per-widget pane_content memory <= capture lines (100 non-focused, 500-1,000 focused) ~ <=6 MB at 200 agents.

Single JSON parse of monitor_daemon_state.json, O(N_AGENTS) entries; 96 us for 9 KB here; per-second use is in worker threads except DaemonPanel (visible-only).

On disk the CSV grows ~35 MB/day (observed 45 MB event_loop_timing.csv) but settings.py:651 cap_diagnostics_csv truncates to the newest 10 % once it passes event_loop_timing_cap_mb (100 MB default), called on every flush (tui.py:4267). Entries added only by user kill (tui.py:3569-3570); removed by cleanup/revive (3605-3607, 3676-3678) and by GC after _TERMINATED_GC_SECONDS=600 s, run from every 5 s _apply_stats_results (tui.py:1900). Max size = kills within a 10-minute window, ~5 KB per Session copy.

pane_content is replaced (not appended) in apply_status_no_refresh (session_summary.py:~230) and holds the same <=100/<=capture_lines lines as the cache, so a second copy of L5 pane bytes (~1.7 MB at 200 agents). Widgets are diffed against display_sessions every update_session_widgets (tui.py:2115-2190 compute_session_widget_diff, widget.remove() for sessions_removed; _execute_kill/_execute_cleanup remove immediately and re-run the diff, tui.py:3576-3585, 3610-3613). Displayed set = non-terminated, non-done sessions of this tmux session (+remote, +<=10 min ghosts when show_terminated) — bounded by N_AGENTS, not N_SESSIONS_TOTAL, because filter_visible_sessions (tui_logic.py:298-309) drops terminated/done unless the user toggles show_terminated (then bounded by terminated entries left in sessions.json — see L5-03).

One set_timer(5.0) per stalled+focused session; the callback pops its own entry (tui.py:2305) and visit/clear paths pop too (2292, 2331); a removed session's timer still fires and pops. All other timers are a fixed set created once in on_mount (tui.py:583-623) plus one set_interval per log-panel widget (tui_log_panel.py:60, daemon_panel.py:39); Textual stores them in a WeakSet (message_pump.py:126) and stops them on unmount (message_pump.py:524-526).

Both guarded by in-progress flags (tui.py:1338-1345, 1539-1541, finally-reset at 1524, 1622) so at most one of each runs. A ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(8, N)) is created and torn down every 250 ms (tui.py:1441) and every 5 s (1573, 1598): up to ~32 thread spawns/s ≈ 2-3 ms/s CPU — wasteful but bounded; a persistent executor would be cleaner.
Replaced wholesale on each reload after a 1 s TTL (tui.py:1117-1120); size == entries in sessions.json; invalidated on refresh (908). Not used by the 4 Hz path (see L5-03).
Ring buffer truncated to MAX_HISTORY=10 (instruction_history_modal.py:18) on every insert (tui.py:3876).
Keyed by a handful of action_key strings ('kill', 'restart', ...); entries overwritten/deleted on each press (session.py:78-89).
Rebuilt from the current widget list on each key press; holds widget references only for currently mounted widgets (navigation.py:91-95).
Explicitly pruned to ids present in self.sessions before persisting (view.py:311-316). Stale ids loaded from an old prefs file survive only until the next toggle.

List replaced on every 10 s poll (tui.py:1648) or element-replaced by the 1.5 s focused poll (1681-1683); SisterState.sessions replaced per poll (sister_poller.py:212); size = remote agents across S_SISTERS. Timeline merge (poll_all_timelines) returns a fresh dict each 30 s that replaces StatusTimeline._agent_histories (status_timeline.py:101-104) — bounded by remote window rows (contributes to L5-04).
Replaced every second with dict(burn.per_session) — one small WindowBurnStats per non-asleep session; no accumulation. (The cost is in computing it, L5-01.)
One entry per remote session with SSH; stale entries deleted when the window is gone (tui.py:2519); cleared on unmount (2572-2579).

log_lines is sliced to the last 100 (tui_log_panel.py:94, daemon_panel.py:76); initial/rotation reads use tail_file_lines with a 256 KB byte cap (daemon_logging.py:34-58); the 1 s timer returns early when the panel is hidden (tui_log_panel.py:63-65). Caveat: when a panel is re-shown after being hidden for a long time, the incremental branch reads everything appended since the saved offset once (bounded by the daemon log's rotation size, ~21 MB observed for monitor_daemon.log.1). _log_to_daemon_panel (tui_actions/daemon.py:16-23) appends without trimming while hidden, but only on explicit user daemon actions.
Appended only on stall notifications; cleared on every flush (notifier.py:48, 63), and flush is called at the end of every 4 Hz apply (tui.py:1881).

bounded_ok.why_bounded: Notifications._reap() drops expired toasts on every add and on len() (notifications.py:79-96); default timeout 5 s; keyed dict so identical notifications dedupe. No unbounded growth even under repeated notify.
Single snapshot object; fetch throttled to 300 s (usage_monitor.py:43, 62) and only when the fleet has a subscription backend (tui.py:642-646).

Gated by _column_widths_dirty (tui.py:1003-1006); dirty is set by the 5 s stats apply and structural updates, so the O(N) render_summary_cells sweep runs ~every 5-10 s, not at 4 Hz. column_widths is a list of ~30 ints.
O(N_AGENTS) dict/set diff plus one get_monitor_daemon_state parse; no retained state beyond widgets. Runs every 10 s from _apply_sessions and on user toggles; bounded by N_AGENTS.
Scalars only; heartbeat write throttled to 5 s (tui.py:4091-4093).

Job widgets diffed and removed when a job disappears (tui.py:2766-2785); pane capture only for the focused job at 1 Hz and only in jobs mode (tui.py:2800-2812); JobSummary.pane_content is a replaced reactive list of visible pane lines. Bounded by J_JOBS and V_TERM.

bounded_ok.function: StatusHistoryFile.read hours-window cache interplay (timeline 3 h vs status bar baseline+0.1 h)

Cache is one reader per path in module dict _readers (229-238) — one entry for this TUI. (The size of that window is L5-04.)
Python ints incremented per tick (4 Hz -> ~2.4 M per week); arbitrary precision, no overflow, no growth of note.
Always returns INTERVAL_FAST (=2 s from settings.py:156); no adaptive logic, so cadence is a constant — this is also why every per-loop site above runs at 0.5 Hz regardless of fleet idleness.
Sleeps in 1 s chunks; one unlink() per second for the activity signal (check_activity_signal 132-150, no exists() pre-check); an extra state.save only when the signal fires.
One O(N) serialisation + fsync + rename per loop (~3 KB/session); supervisor_stats.json read is a tiny file; presence.get_current_state is a heartbeat-file read plus Quartz calls.
Six O(N) sums over in-memory session states per save.

Runs once per daemon lifetime (flag at 1113-1115); one list_windows call.
Dict lookups on the default detector's _last_detect_phase; logs only on phase change (sticky_green phase strings embed the age so can change per loop, but that state lasts <=1.5 s).
O(N) set difference per loop (though it misses several dicts — L6-19, memory only).
O(N) datetime.fromisoformat per loop; writes only on expiry.
Every 60 loops; O(N) pure checks; spawns only per archived agent.
Every 60 loops; one list-sessions + one list-windows spawn; O(K windows in session).
Per-session sends gated by heartbeat_frequency_seconds; O(N) cheap checks per loop.
60 s cadence, O(N * skills) stats, write on change only.
Verified: subprocess-free walk to .git + HEAD read; the git-subprocess fallback (665-697) only fires for unrecognised layouts (L6-22 notes the missing negative cache).

Tail-read window of max(200 KB, 128 KB) with doubling — bounded per call by the size of the last 50 events, not the whole file; it is the per-idle-agent-per-loop CADENCE (L6-07) that makes it costly, not the read itself.
Pure functions over the already-parsed hook_state dict and small tails; O(pending_obligations).
Detector pairs cached per backend name (<=5 backends); get_loaded_skills iterates that small dict.
Module-level _READERS cache keyed by backend name.

One ps spawn per 5 s; O(total processes) parse; BFS depth capped at 6. The unbounded part of that sync is the per-session tmux lookups (L6-10).
20 MB cap with single .1 backup => <=40 MB on disk; stdout goes to DEVNULL (pid_utils.spawn_daemon 216-218) so Rich console output is CPU only.
stdout/stderr -> DEVNULL, reaper thread; no log file growth from console output.

Single stat().

Opt-in, at most once per max_age_days, 15 s socket timeout, atomic tmp+replace, runs on a daemon thread (monitor_daemon.py:1196-1201) with 6 h failure backoff.
Process-level cache; loads once.

TTL + mtime cache (_CONFIG_CACHE_TTL); one stat per TTL window.
Reads one small hook_state_<name>.json (bytes to a few KB) per session per call.
BFS with a seen-set and max_depth=6 over a precomputed index; O(subtree) per session, O(P) index build once per sync.
Same bounded BFS (max_depth 6, seen set); argv match is O(subtree).

Linear over lsof output (listeners of the given pids only); non-darwin returns immediately; one lsof spawn per call (counted in L7-15).
Two directory listings with one exists() per entry; O(skills); write only on change (L7-13).
Set arithmetic over N_AGENTS keys; also bounds previous_states/operation_start_times so they do not grow with U_DAEMON.
Pure per-session check; RMW only when a deadline actually fires.
Every 120 s, pure should_auto_archive per session; spawn + RMW only per archived agent.
Every 120 s; one list-sessions + one list-windows over the overcode session only (not K_TMUX-wide).
With relay unconfigured (default) it sets one string and returns each loop.
300 s throttle recorded before the fetch; 5 s keychain timeout, 10 s HTTP timeout; worker thread; snapshot is a single small object.

Post-c6980b8: one index-backed probe per owned id with LIMIT 500 (_MESSAGE_SCAN_LIMIT), narrow columns only, bodies fetched once per (id,time_updated) with a 50,000-entry cap that drops the oldest half.
Owned-id path is a PK IN lookup; directory fallback adopts only a unique candidate.

Always exactly 2*_DAY_SPAN+1 = 3 candidate directories.
O(N_AGENTS) list scan per call; only becomes a problem when called per history entry (counted in L7-03).

Only for wrapper (container) sessions: 1 + len(owned ids) docker exec calls with 5/10 s timeouts per 60 s; `cat` of the container transcript is O(T_TRANSCRIPT) per 60 s with NO cache — same shape as L7-05 but limited to container agents, so listed here as bounded-by-population rather than as a separate site.
Dict lookup into a per-process _READERS registry.
30 s TTL cache per instance; one list-sessions per instance per 30 s. (The instances themselves are recreated per sync — see L7-14/15/19.)

O(capture) only: strip_ansi once (:143), _filter_status_bar_for_hash split+2 startswith per line (:485-503), hash of last 100 lines (:271-272), _detect_approval any() over all lines (:312), spawn-failure on last 20 lines (:519); every other phase runs on last_lines (≤10) or a 6-line joined string. creates ≤1 (polling, hooks) detector pair per backend name; dict lookup afterwards

≤1 entry per PreToolUse of an arming tool; non-persistent kinds removed on PostToolUse by tool_use_id or LIFO by kind (:198-215); persistent cron/schedule_wakeup removed by CronDelete/UserPromptSubmit/SessionEnd (:162-168, :217-223). ≤8 threads created and joined per 250 ms tick regardless of N (~0.5 ms overhead); other lane

sorted() over work_times, whose length is the number of user prompts in the agent's sids (≤ T_TRANSCRIPT turns, ~5,000) → ~1 ms; only web_api.py:490 calls it per request, the TUI does not.

Dict lookup + a few regexes per call (summary_columns.py:558/566/580/1152 per row render); fallback model_metadata.context_window -> active_catalog() is TTL-cached 5 s (model_metadata.py:328 _ACTIVE_TTL_SECONDS = 5.0) and re-stats only 2 candidate files per expiry (:339-345); bundled snapshot is lru_cache(maxsize=1) (:277).

incidents.title: Burn-rate column (#174) re-parses every agent transcript + subagent file from scratch every 1 s (no cache) — most likely the '110% CPU for 15 h' site
incidents.problem: Not a fix: this commit introduced the site. compute_window_burn (tui_logic.py:533-600) runs inside the 1 s update_daemon_status worker (timer tui.py:605 -> _fetch_daemon_status_async tui.py:634-676 -> daemon_status_bar.fetch_volatile_state daemon_status_bar.py:62-104) whenever baseline_minutes > 0, and the default is 60 (settings.py:758, applied tui.py:380). For every non-asleep local agent it calls read_window_token_usage (history_reader.py:1228-1287) on EVERY owned session id (up to _MAX_AGENT_SESSION_IDS=20 incl. cleared sessions) AND every subagent file (get_session_window_token_usage history_reader.py:1290-1355): full open + json.loads of every line, no mtime cache, no byte offset, no result cache (`since` moves each second so a naive result cache cannot hit). Docstring: 'Safe for the typical 5-15 session range; cache externally if you have hundreds.' Cost at reference: sum of all visible agents' transcript bytes parsed once per second; 10 agents x 20 MB = 200 MB/s of JSON ~ >100% of a core continuously while the TUI is open. At T_TRANSCRIPT=200 MB one agent alone exceeds 1 s per pass; the exclusive thread worker then runs back-to-back, pinning a core and contending for the GIL with the 250 ms fast path. Cliff: sum of transcript bytes across visible agents >~ 30-50 MB (~1 s of parse per 1 s tick).
incidents.fix: None so far. a198da9 (Aug 2026) cached the sibling read_session_file_stats (5 s path) but left this reader uncached; c6980b8 fixed the opencode reader that this same 1 Hz path hammers. Freshness need: a 1 h moving-window $/hr in the status bar; a per-file cache of (mtime,size)->list of (timestamp, usage) for assistant messages, appended incrementally from a saved byte offset, then window-summed per call, keeps the 1 s refresh at O(messages in window) instead of O(all bytes). Also codex/grok get_window_token_usage (codex_stats.py:476 _scan_rollout, grok_stats.py:375 _scan_updates) appear to be full-file scans per call on the same 1 Hz path (not profiled); hermes bounds its sampler (hermes_stats.py:97-100, 2000 samples/2 h).
incidents.residual_risk: Fully open. history_reader.py:1228-1287 has no cache; tui_logic.py:571 calls it per session per 1 s tick; daemon_status_bar.py:96-104 gates only on burn_hours > 0 (default 60 min).

incidents.title: Daemon loop 10 s -> 2 s (#291) multiplied an unconditional per-agent full rewrite of the global sessions.json (N x (3 parses + 1 json.dump) per loop)
incidents.problem: Loop shortened 5x for status freshness; per-loop work was never made proportional. In _detect_and_enrich (monitor_daemon.py:1365-1474) each agent per loop: refresh_git_context -> get_session -> _load_state (full json.load of ~/.overcode/sessions/sessions.json, session_manager.py:718-741, 825-830), update_stats(current_task=...) unconditionally (monitor_daemon.py:1408-1411 -> session_manager.py:971-977 -> _locked_state read + json.dump(indent=2) of the ENTIRE file under LOCK_EX, session_manager.py:545-597), then get_session again (monitor_daemon.py:1417). sessions.json is one global file shared by every tmux session/daemon (M_MULTI). At N_SESSIONS_TOTAL=2000 entries (~3.4 KB/entry measured from archive.json => ~7 MB with indent=2) and N=50: 50 x (3 x ~50 ms parse + ~120 ms dump) ~ 13 s of work per 2 s loop — the daemon cannot finish a loop, TUI shows it stale, and the TUI's LOCK_SH reads (4 Hz) block behind LOCK_EX writers. Present since 02b64a1; flagged as 'Full JSON state rewrite every daemon cycle' in docs/ux-performance-analysis-2026-03-09.md:48 and never fixed. Cliff: N_AGENTS x size(sessions.json) >~ 8 agent-MB per loop (e.g. 8 agents with a 1 MB file, ~300 entries).
incidents.fix: 2c1c388 set INTERVAL_FAST=2 (settings.py:156), TUI daemon-state read 1 s, single-pass read_session_file_stats. Freshness need: status 2 s (keep). Fix that keeps it: compare-before-write (skip update_stats when current_task unchanged), batch all per-loop session mutations into one _locked_state, read sessions.json once per loop and pass the in-memory Session through instead of get_session reloads; prune terminated/archived entries out of sessions.json.
incidents.residual_risk: Open: monitor_daemon.py:1408 update_stats is unconditional; session_manager.py:975 has no change check; session_manager.py:587-589 dumps whole state on every context exit.
incidents.degradation_note: Reverse case: freshness improved 5x (10 s -> 2 s) at 5x the per-loop cost.

incidents.title: Fast/slow path split (250 ms / 5 s) — fast path still json.load()s sessions.json and monitor_daemon_state.json 4x/s with no mtime gate
incidents.problem: Split heavy stats off the 250 ms path (later 514eb06 merged the 250 ms/1 s timers into one 250 ms timer). The remaining 250 ms path (tui.py:1329-1345 -> _fetch_statuses_async 1363-1400) calls session_manager.list_sessions() (full json.load of the global sessions.json, session_manager.py:421-460, 840-845) and get_monitor_daemon_state (json.load, monitor_daemon_state.py:288-305) every tick with no stat() gate. Additional parses of sessions.json: 1 Hz x2 in daemon status (tui.py:656, daemon_status_bar.py:98), 0.2 Hz stats (tui.py:1546), 0.2 Hz summaries (1973), 0.1 Hz refresh -> ~6.4 parses/s. Native sample 2026-09-20 showed json scanstring as top TUI symbol at only 22 KB/4 entries. At 2000 entries (~7 MB) that is ~45 MB/s of json.load ~ 40-60% of a core. Cliff: sessions.json >~ 1 MB (~300 entries) => 4 Hz parse ~10% core; >~ 5 MB => a full core.
incidents.fix: Fast/slow split kept; timer starvation fixed (514eb06). Freshness need: focused status 250 ms — but the sessions.json read only supplies fields (asleep, status, tmux_window) that change rarely; stat() mtime+size gate on both files (parse only on change) preserves 250 ms fidelity. Note the gate only pays off once the daemon stops rewriting unchanged data N times per loop (see 2c1c388 incident).
incidents.residual_risk: Open: tui.py:1371 and 1382 read both files unconditionally each tick; session_manager.py:439 and monitor_daemon_state.py:303 have no caching.

incidents.title: hook_events_<name>.jsonl 'rotation' (#448) is by lines not bytes — once lines average >512 B every hook event rewrites the whole file
incidents.problem: Introduced the append-only per-agent event log so fast hook bursts survive polling, with a rotation: when size > _EVENT_LOG_ROTATE_BYTES=100 KB (hook_handler.py:333) keep the last _EVENT_LOG_KEEP_LINES=200 (334) via readlines()+rewrite (337-354), checked after every append (386-391). Events carry the full tool_input (hook_handler.py:769, untruncated Write/Edit payloads). Measured here: hook_events_bobbit.jsonl = 1,426,096 B with exactly 200 lines (avg 7.1 KB, max 9 KB). Once the last 200 lines exceed 100 KB the file can never drop under the threshold, so EVERY subsequent hook event does append -> stat -> readlines() of 1.4 MB -> rewrite 1.4 MB, in the hook handler's critical path (adds latency to every tool call) and at R_HOOKS=5/s ~ 15 MB/s of I/O fleet-wide. Reader side: _read_recent_events (hook_status_detector.py:487-538) starts with a 200 KB window (limit 50 x 4096) and doubles until 50 lines fit — with 7 KB lines that is up to ~800 KB read+decode per Stop-event detection (daemon N per 2 s; TUI focused 4 Hz + 1-in-4 rotation). Cliff: mean event line > 512 B (any agent using Write/Edit).
incidents.fix: a198da9 bounded the READ side (tail window) but the write-side bound is broken. Freshness need: sticky-green needs the last ~50 events' event+timestamp+tool_name only. Fix: store a short tool label instead of tool_input, rotate by bytes (keep last ~64 KB) and read the tail by bytes — no fidelity loss.
incidents.residual_risk: Open: hook_handler.py:333-354 line-based trim vs byte threshold; hook_handler.py:769 appends full tool_input; verified on disk (200-line, 1.4 MB file).

incidents.problem: TUI 5 s stats sweep re-parsed every Claude session JSONL for every agent each cycle (one old agent: 115 MB / 15 static files ~ 356 ms JSON per 5 s, pinned a core; independent of agent count). _read_recent_events slurped whole hook_events_*.jsonl via readlines() per detection.
incidents.fix: _session_stats_cache keyed (path, mtime, size, since), capped at _SESSION_STATS_CACHE_MAX=512 with drop-oldest-half (history_reader.py:923-988); _read_recent_events bounded tail window with doubling (hook_status_detector.py:487-538). Output-identical, no cadence change.
incidents.residual_risk: Partially open. (1) Cache is all-or-nothing per file: the ACTIVE transcript changes every turn so each 5 s sweep (tui.py:604 -> 1528-1620) and each 60 s daemon sync_agent_stats re-parse it in full (_parse_session_lines full pass, history_reader.py:979-981); at T_TRANSCRIPT=200 MB that is ~2-4 s of json.loads per 5 s per active agent; cliff ~20-30 MB active transcript per agent (~0.3-0.5 s per parse, 10% core each). Fix keeping 5 s freshness: incremental parse from a saved byte offset (append-only file) with running totals + last-N work times. (2) Sibling read_window_token_usage got no cache and runs at 1 Hz (see 8103d03). (3) _SESSION_STATS_CACHE_MAX=512 (history_reader.py:931): main + cleared sessions (<=20 ids) + subagent files per agent means 50 agents x ~11 files > 512 => drop-oldest-half thrash and static files get re-parsed again; cliff ~512 distinct transcript files across the fleet.

incidents.title: HistoryFile mtime cache for ~/.claude/history.jsonl + staggered 5 s timers — TUI constructs a fresh HistoryFile() every sweep so history.jsonl is fully parsed every 5 s regardless of change
incidents.problem: history.jsonl (one line per user prompt across ALL Claude Code sessions on the machine; 3.4 MB / 8,500 lines here, ~40 MB / 100k lines at P_CLAUDE_PROJECTS reference) was parsed N times per 5 s cycle.
incidents.fix: HistoryFile with mtime+size cache (history_reader.py:479-536), one shared instance per stats cycle, module singleton _default_history (704); 5 s timers staggered +1.7 s/+3.3 s (tui.py:605,609).
incidents.residual_risk: Open. (1) tui.py:1550 `history_file = HistoryFile()` creates a new instance per 5 s sweep (_cached_mtime=0) so the cache never carries across sweeps: full json.loads of every line every 5 s (~0.4-0.8 s per sweep at 100k lines ~ 8-16% core, plus rebuilding 100k HistoryEntry objects -> GC churn). The daemon's _default_history singleton does cache. (2) Even when cached, _entries() (history_reader.py:502-536) re-parses the whole file on any change (append-only, no offset), and it changes on every prompt fleet-wide. (3) get_interactions_for_session (567-580) walks all entries per agent; for legacy agents without agent_session_ids it calls Path(entry.project).resolve() (realpath syscall) per entry => N x 100k syscalls per sweep. Freshness need 5 s; fix: use the singleton + incremental tail parse from saved offset + per-sessionId index.

incidents.title: 0.5.4: cut tmux/subprocess load (focused-only 4 Hz capture, 1-in-4 rotation, resize/list_sessions/git dedupe, hook-handler fast path)
incidents.problem: tmux server is single-threaded; TUI captured every agent every 250 ms (4N cmds/s; at 20 agents display-message p90 went 4 -> 15 ms), 15 s resize sweep sent N resize-window (not a no-op), list_sessions 2 tmux cmds/agent per 10 s, git diff+untracked subprocesses per agent per 5 s, daemon 2 git subprocesses per agent per 2 s, hook-handler ~80 ms of imports per hook event.
incidents.fix: tui_logic.select_capture_sessions (focused + daemon-unknown every tick, others 1-in-NON_FOCUSED_CAPTURE_EVERY=4, tui_logic.py:920-944; call site tui.py:1397-1427), windows_needing_resize (946-963; tui.py:822-880 one list-windows), launcher.list_sessions one list_windows(include_command=False), should_scan_git every 3rd sweep deduped per directory (tui_logic.py:963-975; tui.py:1552-1575), read_git_context_from_disk, entrypoint.py fast path (~20 ms/event).
incidents.residual_risk: Partially open. (1) TUI still issues 1 + N/4 capture-pane per 250 ms tick = ~N captures/s (tui_logic.py:938-943): 50/s at N=50, 200/s at N=200; agents absent from daemon state are captured every tick (941). Cliff ~150 agents where 3-6 ms per tmux command saturates the server (plus daemon load below). (2) Daemon untouched: N captures of 550 lines per 2 s (monitor_daemon.py:1380 -> status_detector.py:95-96 / hook_status_detector.py:655; DEFAULT_CAPTURE_LINES=500 status_constants.py:16). (3) Daemon _sync_process_resources (5 s) and _sync_sandbox_state (15 s) build a throwaway RealTmux() per call (monitor_daemon.py:1274, 1332) so the 30 s pane cache is always cold: ~3 tmux cmds per agent per lookup => ~0.8N tmux cmds/s (40/s at N=50, 160/s at N=200). (4) TUI fast path ThreadPoolExecutor(max 8) issues captures concurrently, so bursts of up to 8 simultaneous tmux clients per tick.
incidents.degradation_note: Focused agent unchanged (250 ms). Non-focused agents: pane-derived columns (activity text, PR number, last pane text) now refresh ~1 s and status comes from daemon state (2 s fresh) instead of 250 ms; git diff/untracked columns lag up to 15 s instead of 5 s. Both within what those columns need.

incidents.title: #352 quick wins: 100-line captures for non-focused TUI agents, precompiled regex, single strip_ansi, tree metadata gated
incidents.problem: 550-line captures for all agents 4x/s; regex recompiled per call; 3+ strip_ansi passes per widget per tick; compute_tree_metadata O(N*depth) every tick even when not in tree sort.
incidents.fix: STATUS_CAPTURE_LINES=100 for non-focused (status_constants.py:17; tui.py:1425), patterns precompiled in status_patterns.py, strip once in extract_from_pane, compute_child_counts O(N) unless by_tree.
incidents.residual_risk: Daemon never got the reduced capture: monitor_daemon.py:1380 detect_status(session) with num_lines=0 -> capture_lines(500)+50 = 550 lines per agent per 2 s (status_detector.py:86-96), while detection looks at the last 10-40 lines (status_detector.py:150, hook_status_detector.py:74,96) and the daemon publishes no pane text (only extract_pr_number reads it). Per 2026-09-20 measurement a 550-line capture is ~6 ms vs ~3.3 ms at 100 lines: the daemon's tmux time per loop is ~2x what it needs. TUI focused capture = max(500, 2 x terminal height) (tui.py:882-885) — bounded by V_TERM.
incidents.degradation_note: Non-focused status detection sees 100 lines instead of 550; detection uses <=40 lines so nothing visible was lost.

incidents.title: Per-agent CPU/RAM sampler: one ps -eo per 5 s plus a cold tmux pane lookup per agent per 5 s (and per 15 s for sandbox)
incidents.problem: Added _sync_process_resources every 5 s (monitor_daemon.py:1254-1311): snapshot_processes runs `ps -eo pid,ppid,%cpu,rss,args` for the whole machine (process_resources.py:29-40) and, per agent, tmux.get_pane_pid + find_agent_process + aggregate_tree; writes sessions.json only when CPU moves >=1% or RSS >=1 MiB. _sync_sandbox_state (1313-1355, 15 s) does the same ps snapshot + lsof + per-agent pane lookup.
incidents.fix: Change-gated writes (1298-1306) limit sessions.json churn for idle agents only.
incidents.residual_risk: Open: `tmux = RealTmux()` is constructed fresh per call (monitor_daemon.py:1274, 1332), so RealTmux's 30 s cache (implementations.py:30-107) never hits: each get_pane_pid = sessions.get + windows.get + panes ~ 3 tmux commands => ~0.6N cmds/s (resources) + ~0.2N (sandbox); 40/s at N=50, 160/s at N=200 — same order as the capture load a96ff0f removed. Any active agent whose RSS drifts >1 MiB between samples triggers a full sessions.json rewrite every 5 s (see 2c1c388 incident). ps output ∝ machine process count (~200 KB parse per 5 s at 2k procs: fine). Fix: reuse one RealTmux (or one list-panes with #{pane_pid} for the whole session per sweep).

incidents.title: #372 audit perf: config TTL cache, column-width dirty flag, presence CSV mtime cache, terminated-session GC
incidents.problem: load_config parsed YAML per call; column widths O(N x C) per 250 ms; read_presence_history re-parsed the CSV each read; _terminated_sessions grew unbounded over TUI uptime.
incidents.fix: config.py:20-60 TTL 5 s + mtime; tui.py:297,1000-1014 _column_widths_dirty; presence_logger.py:395-450 mtime+size+hours cache; tui.py:393 _TERMINATED_GC_SECONDS=600 with _gc_terminated_sessions (1884-1896) run from _apply_stats_results.
incidents.residual_risk: Config cache, dirty flag and terminated GC verified bounded. Presence is still open: the mtime cache never hits in steady state because the presence logger (runs inside the daemon) appends a row every DEFAULT_SAMPLE_INTERVAL=60 s (presence_logger.py:60, 262-330), so the 30 s timeline refresh (tui.py:607 -> status_timeline.py:91) re-parses the WHOLE ~/.overcode/presence_log.csv with csv.DictReader + fromisoformat per row after every write, keeping only the last `hours`. No rotation anywhere in presence_logger.py (0 matches). 12 MB here (~100k rows) ~ 150-300 ms per parse every 60 s, growing linearly with daemon wall-clock forever. web_api.py:620,777 read it per request too. Fix keeping 30 s freshness: binary seek to cutoff (status_history.py:145 already implements this pattern) + incremental tail + rotation.

incidents.title: #465/#468: hourly gzip rotation of agent_status_history.csv (>50 MB or >7 d, keep newest 30 h), 540 d retention, event_loop_timing.csv 100 MB cap
incidents.problem: agent_status_history.csv append-only (~40 MB/day reported, 2.4 GB / 21M rows in the field); event_loop_timing.csv append-only at 10 rows/s (~35 MB/day).
incidents.fix: status_history.py:341-344 (DEFAULT_ROTATE_MB=50, 7 d, ROTATION_KEEP_HOURS=30), rotate_and_retain (525-546) called hourly from monitor_daemon.py:1128-1157; cap_diagnostics_csv (settings.py:651-680, seek-based drop of oldest 90%) from tui.py:4271.
incidents.residual_risk: Growth is bounded but the bound is set by N_AGENTS x 30 h, not 50 MB: rotation keeps every row younger than keep_hours=30 h (status_history.py:395-426), and the daemon writes one row per agent per 2 s loop unconditionally, even when status is unchanged (monitor_daemon.py:1460 log_agent_status). At ~80 B/row: 12 agents already fill 50 MB in 30 h, N=50 => ~216 MB permanent active file, N=200 => ~860 MB. Because it stays over 50 MB, rotation fires EVERY hour and streams+gzips the whole file synchronously inside the daemon loop (monitor_daemon.py:1125 -> 1141-1148): seconds at N=50, ~minute at N=200 of no status detection ('daemon stale' in the TUI) each hour. Readers stay proportional to hours requested (binary seek), so read cost is fine. Fix with no fidelity loss (timeline resolution is 30 s): log only on status/activity change plus a periodic keepalive row, and run rotation on a thread like model metadata (cedd8bd). event_loop_timing cap verified bounded (100 MB; trips every ~3 days; the trim reads/rewrites ~10 MB on the main loop in _flush_heartbeat — ~50-100 ms stall).

incidents.title: #468/#465: streaming history rotation (no full materialisation); cap status_changes.csv
incidents.problem: rotate_status_history loaded every row of a 2.4 GB / 21M-row CSV into Python lists before writing archive + trimmed file — would OOM the daemon on first rotation after upgrade. status_changes.csv (opt-in diagnostic) append-only for TUI lifetime.
incidents.fix: Single streaming pass to two temp files with gzip level 6 (status_history.py:384-492); cap_diagnostics_csv on status_changes.csv (tui.py:4299-4302).
incidents.residual_risk: Memory bounded (streaming). Still synchronous in the daemon loop (_maybe_rotate_history monitor_daemon.py:1128-1157 from _tick:1125): the one-off legacy migration of a multi-GB file stalls status detection for minutes, and at N>=12 agents rotation recurs hourly (see 9115368).

incidents.title: 0.5.4 #476: opencode/opencode2 stats readers — per-conversation index probes + bounded per-row parse cache (declined 60 s TTL cache)
incidents.problem: `session_id IN (...) ORDER BY ... LIMIT 500*N` built a temp B-tree over all candidate rows (quadratic in owned ids: 2 ms at 1 id, 115 ms at 8) and opencode2 re-fetched + json.loads'd 500 inline tool-output bodies (>1 MB tail) per conversation per call; called 1 Hz (burn) + 5 s (stats) per agent.
incidents.fix: One bounded index-ordered probe per conversation merged in Python; narrow-column probes plus _row_cache keyed (store, table, id, time_updated), _ROW_CACHE_MAX=50_000 with drop-oldest-half (opencode_stats.py:365-440); in-flight rows never cached. 2.3 GB store, 8 ids: opencode2 254 -> 9.6 ms, opencode 23 -> 6.7 ms.
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: cache capped at 50k entries (opencode_stats.py:365, eviction 436-439) => <= ~10-25 MB; per-session scan limit 500 rows. Eviction is insertion-order not LRU, so with >25k hot rows (>=50 opencode agents x 500) half the working set churns per overflow — a re-fetch cost, not growth. The path is still driven at 1 Hz per agent by the burn-rate site (8103d03).

incidents.title: PR #467: rotate monitor_daemon.log at 20 MB; log panels tail 256 KB instead of readlines() of the whole file
incidents.problem: monitor_daemon.log append-only (238 MB / 6 months); TUI daemon and tui log panels read the entire file every 1 s to keep 100 lines -> ~800 MB RSS spikes.
incidents.fix: BaseDaemonLogger._maybe_rotate to single .1 backup past MAX_LOG_BYTES=20 MB (daemon_logging.py:31,75-86); tail_file_lines reads last 256 KB (34-58) with incremental file_pos and re-tail after shrink; used by daemon_panel.py:66 and tui_log_panel.py:83.
incidents.residual_risk: Daemon log verified bounded at 40 MB per tmux session (5.2 MB + 20 MB .1 here); log volume ∝ R_HOOKS since 8ffb485 logs every hook-event change (bounded by rotation). Still open: tui.log uses a plain logging.FileHandler at DEBUG with no rotation (tui_log_panel.py:23-45) — slow growth (60 KB here) but unbounded over U_TUI. Both panels re-read up to 256 KB every 1 s even when unchanged (no mtime gate; file_pos limits it to new bytes in the steady state, so acceptable).

incidents.title: #473: model-metadata auto-refresh moved off the daemon loop onto a thread
incidents.problem: Hourly synchronous urlopen with 60 s timeout inside the monitor loop: on a packet-dropping network, a 1-minute stall of status detection every hour (TUI showed daemon stale).
incidents.fix: Fetch runs on a daemon thread; loop only checks in-flight (monitor_daemon.py:1159-1222, thread at 1195); timeout 15 s; 6 h backoff on failure.
incidents.residual_risk: Verified: threading.Thread at monitor_daemon.py:1195, gated by should_sync_stats hourly (1171-1173). Fully fixed for this site; history rotation (6a10756/9115368) did not get the same treatment.

incidents.title: StatusHistoryFile: binary-seek + incremental tail reads of agent_status_history.csv (368k rows was ~300 ms GIL-bound per read at 5 s/30 s)
incidents.problem: agent_status_history.csv re-parsed from scratch every 5 s (status bar spin rate) and 30 s (timeline): ~300 ms CPU, ~600 ms event-loop stalls.
incidents.fix: StatusHistoryFile singleton per path (status_history.py:59-235): _seek_to_cutoff binary search (145-186), _incremental_read from saved offset when file grew (128-142), full re-read only on shrink or larger `hours`.
incidents.residual_risk: Read cost bounded (∝ rows within `hours`). Memory is not independent of N_AGENTS: _cached_entries holds every row within the largest hours requested; at 0.5 rows/s/agent (daemon logs unchanged status every loop) N=50 x 3 h = 270k tuples (~40 MB), 24 h timeline at N=200 = 8.6M tuples (~1.3 GB). The status bar calls read(hours=baseline/60+0.1) every 1 s (daemon_status_bar.py:79) and _filter walks the whole cached list each call (~99k tuples/s at N=50, 400k/s at N=200). Root cause is the unconditional row per agent per loop (monitor_daemon.py:1460).

incidents.title: #161: RealTmux 30 s pane/session cache + tiered 250 ms focused / 1 s background updates (5 agents were ~100 forks/s)
incidents.problem: libtmux spawned ~5 subprocesses per capture_pane (session/window/pane lookups); 5 agents x 4 Hz = ~100 forks/s.
incidents.fix: RealTmux _pane_cache/_session_cache with _CACHE_TTL=30 (implementations.py:30-107): 1 tmux command per capture in steady state; tiered updates (646c6c6). 514eb06 then merged the tiers into one 250 ms timer with every-4th-tick inclusion; by 0.5.3 all agents were captured every tick again (docstring tui.py:1330 'Update all session statuses every 250ms'), and a96ff0f re-introduced the 1-in-4 rotation.
incidents.residual_risk: Cache verified per instance; _pane_cache is never evicted except invalidate_cache (grows with distinct (session, window) pairs seen over process uptime — tiny objects, effectively bounded by K_TMUX). Open: several daemon paths build throwaway RealTmux() instances (monitor_daemon.py:953, 968, 1274, 1332) so their lookups are always cold (see 6dff292 incident).
incidents.degradation_note: Background agents at ~1 Hz instead of 4 Hz; their status text tolerates 1-2 s. The tiering was silently lost later and only restored in a96ff0f.

incidents.title: #116: session-id detection reads the last 64 KB of history.jsonl backwards with a per-directory mtime cache; daemon id-sync 10 s / stats-sync 60 s split
incidents.problem: get_current_session_id_for_directory parsed all of history.jsonl per agent per daemon loop (9.8 ms cold at the time).
incidents.fix: _read_lines_reversed 64 KB tail (history_reader.py:675-702), _session_id_cache keyed by directory + mtime/size (595-643); monitor_daemon.py:326-327 _session_id_sync_interval=10, 322-323 _stats_sync_interval=60.
incidents.residual_risk: Fast path verified bounded (cache <= N directories; 64 KB re-read per agent per 10 s when history.jsonl changed). Open sibling: the zero-token slow path discover_session_ids (monitor_daemon.py:713-721 -> stats_reader.py:150-186) constructs a fresh HistoryFile() and read_all()s the entire history.jsonl per such agent every 10 s — with k idle/new agents that is k full parses of a 100k-line file per 10 s.

incidents.title: #222: move blocking I/O (pgrep, daemon state JSON, CSV parsing, session JSON, log tailing) off the Textual main loop
incidents.problem: 3-second GUI freezes from file I/O, subprocesses and CSV parsing on the main thread.
incidents.fix: update_daemon_status, refresh_sessions, update_timeline, DaemonPanel/TuiLogPanel and DaemonStatusBar.fetch_volatile_state run under @work(thread=True) (tui.py:634, 734, 895; daemon_panel.py:49; tui_log_panel.py:69).
incidents.residual_risk: Mostly verified. Residual main-thread I/O: _poll_focused_job_pane (1 s timer tui.py:619 -> 2811-2826) calls pane.capture_pane() (tmux subprocess) synchronously in jobs mode (tui.py:2806); _flush_heartbeat/_flush_status_changes (5 s timers) append files and run cap_diagnostics_csv on the main loop (tui.py:4254-4302) — a ~10 MB read/rewrite (~50-100 ms) each time the 100 MB cap trips (~every 3 days). Moving heavy work to threads also made the work invisible in the UI while still costing CPU (the 8103d03 site pins a core inside a worker).

incidents.title: Usage monitor API poll 90 s -> 5 min
incidents.problem: Claude usage-limit fetch (subprocess/HTTP) every 90 s from the 1 s daemon-status worker.
incidents.fix: _min_interval=300 (usage_monitor.py:43, 50-62); later gated by _fleet_has_subscription_usage (tui.py:678-690).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: one throttled fetch per 300 s (usage_monitor.py:62).
incidents.degradation_note: Usage bar (5 h / 7 d limits) can lag up to 5 min instead of 90 s; the numbers change slowly and 38dd9ff shows the last-queried age, so acceptable.

incidents.title: #10: monitor daemon must always poll at the fast interval (maintainer stance: adaptive slow-down loses monitoring resolution)
incidents.problem: Daemon reduced polling frequency when agents idle, losing resolution.
incidents.fix: calculate_interval always returns INTERVAL_FAST (monitor_daemon.py:909-917); later 10 s -> 2 s in 2c1c388.
incidents.residual_risk: Verified: no adaptive interval; interval_slow/idle in settings.py:157-158 are unused by the monitor daemon. Establishes that fixes must not slow the loop.

incidents.title: AI summarizer moved from daemon to TUI (#123); later idle auto-pause + cost cap (389e24b)
incidents.problem: Summarizer API calls and pane captures ran in the daemon even with no viewer.
incidents.fix: SummarizerComponent in TUI under _update_summaries_async (tui.py:1930-1980): returns unless enabled, pauses after idle_timeout with no keypress, halts at cost cap; content-hash gating (summarizer_component.py:94-183).
incidents.residual_risk: Bounded by opt-in and idle pause. When enabled it still captures every agent's pane every 5 s (summarizer_component.py:167, N/5 tmux cmds/s) and parses sessions.json again (tui.py:1973); the hash only saves API calls. Never profiled (noted in the 2026-09-20 investigation) but off by default.

incidents.title: Status-change diagnostics gated behind status_change_logging (default off)
incidents.problem: Raw status tracking, phase/source dicts and a 5 s flush timer ran for every session every tick.
incidents.fix: All gated on self._prefs.status_change_logging (tui.py:1438-1445, 1471; timer only set at 586 when enabled); CSV capped when on (6a10756).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: off by default; when on, status_changes.csv capped at 100 MB (tui.py:4299-4302).

incidents.title: PR #467: TUI `q` exits the viewer (was detach-only, leaving ~19% CPU burning unwatched)
incidents.problem: In split mode `q` detached the tmux client but left `overcode monitor` running.
incidents.fix: action_quit detaches then self.exit(); cli/split.py wraps the pane in a hold-and-relaunch shell (~0% CPU).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified. Does nothing for a TUI left attached (the 15 h report); the memory note (project_q_quit_stop_restart.md) shows the maintainer wants q to stop the viewer, which this does.
incidents.degradation_note: Re-attach now requires a relaunch (one keypress) and loses in-memory TUI state (terminated-session cache, summaries); acceptable trade for zero idle CPU.

incidents.title: #396 jobs: skip kill detection on empty list_windows, 30 s grace — jobs refresh cost scales with running jobs
incidents.problem: Jobs falsely marked killed on stale libtmux cache.
incidents.fix: job_launcher.py:101-160 guard + grace; jobs TUI refresh 5 s (fb2473d).
incidents.residual_risk: Bounded but linear in J_JOBS: every 5 s (tui.py:617 -> 2745, worker thread) one list_windows plus, per RUNNING job, tmux get_pane_pid + a `pgrep`-style _has_child_processes subprocess (job_launcher.py:150-152, 215-224) => 50 running jobs = 10 subprocesses/s + tmux lookups; jobs.json (job_manager.py:122) keeps completed jobs forever and is parsed each refresh.

incidents.title: opencode/opencode2 stats readers: quadratic IN+ORDER BY+LIMIT query and full row-body parse per call
incidents.problem: TUI daemon-status worker recomputed window burn for every awake opencode agent at 1 Hz and get_stats per agent per 5 s sweep. Each call ran one `WHERE session_id IN (...) ORDER BY time_created DESC LIMIT 500*N` (temp B-tree over all candidate rows, ~N^2 in owned conversation ids: 2 ms at 1 id -> 117 ms at 8) and JSON-parsed up to 500 message bodies per conversation (median 1 KB, p90 9 KB, tail >1 MB). Measured 75 ms (window) / 115 ms (stats) per agent on a 1.9 GB store; GIL-holding work starved the input loop (typing lag when switching agents). The user's proposed 60 s TTL cache was declined.
incidents.fix: c6980b8: one bounded, index-ordered probe per conversation merged in Python (no outer SQL sort), narrow-column select so overflow pages are never read, plus a per-row parse cache keyed (store, table, id, time_updated), bounded at 50,000 entries with half-drop eviction; in-flight assistant rows never cached. opencode2 get_stats 254 ms -> 9.6 ms on a 2.3 GB generated store. Freshness kept at 5 s (TUI) / 1 s (burn).
incidents.residual_risk: Query shape is bounded (500 rows x owned ids per call; owned ids capped at 20 by hook_handler.py:260 _MAX_AGENT_SESSION_IDS). Row cache bounded at 50,000 entries (opencode_stats.py:365-440); memory per entry not measured. Design doc open questions (docs/design/opencode-stats-reader-performance.md:226-231) note the TUI still calls get_stats per agent per 5 s in addition to the daemon's 60 s sync, and that the Claude backend's read_window_token_usage has the same 1 Hz cadence with NO cache (see separate incident). Not verified against the reporter's 1.9 GB store.
incidents.degradation_note: Same work done cheaper; the declined TTL patch would have dropped opencode stats freshness 5 s -> 60 s.

incidents.title: agent_status_history.csv grew without bound (2.4 GB / 21M rows, filled a shared disk)
incidents.problem: monitor daemon appends one row per agent per loop (status_history.py:18 log_agent_status; loop = INTERVAL_FAST 2 s, settings.py:156). No rotation/retention; on a 2-month multi-agent devpod reached 2.4 GB and took the host filesystem to 100%. event_loop_timing.csv reached 3.7 GB the same way.
incidents.fix: 9115368: hourly check (monitor_daemon.py:1128-1157 _maybe_rotate_history) rotates the active CSV once >50 MB or oldest row >7 days: rows older than 30 h go to <name>.<ts>.csv.gz (gzip ~15-20x), archives pruned after 540 days (configurable history_retention in docs/configuration.md:307-340); web analytics range endpoint reads archives. 6a10756: rotation streams row-by-row (status_history.py:384-470) instead of loading the file into memory (which would have OOM-killed the daemon on the reported file). Downsampling was NOT done.
incidents.residual_risk: Disk is bounded per active file but total archive volume still grows with N_AGENTS x W_WALLCLOCK: at N=50 the write rate is 25 rows/s (~2.2M rows, ~200 MB/day, rotating ~4x/day) -> ~10-13 MB/day gzipped -> ~5-7 GB over the 540-day retention; N=200 -> ~25 GB. Maintainer caveat: the one-off rotation of a legacy multi-GB file blocks the daemon loop for minutes (no status updates meanwhile). The in-memory reader side (StatusHistoryFile window cache, status_history.py:59-235) scales with N_AGENTS x window hours - see the #284 incident. Local machine: active file is 22.4 MB with .csv.gz archives up to 175 MB, consistent with rotation working.
incidents.degradation_note: All rows retained (compressed); windowed readers unaffected. Per-loop row cadence unchanged.

incidents.title: diagnostics/event_loop_timing.csv and status_changes.csv chewed disk (3.7 GB)
incidents.problem: TUI heartbeat probe records every ~100 ms (tui.py:583 set_interval(0.1, _record_heartbeat)) and flushes every 5 s; opt-in status_changes.csv likewise; neither was capped.
incidents.fix: cap_diagnostics_csv (settings.py:651-680): after each 5 s flush, stat the file and if >event_loop_timing_cap_mb (default 100 MB) keep only the newest ~10% via seek+rewrite; event_loop_timing_enabled:false disables the probe. Applied in _flush_heartbeat (tui.py:4254-4272) and _flush_status_changes (tui.py:4284-4302).
incidents.residual_risk: Bounded at 100 MB per file. Note both flushes and the cap run in a Textual timer callback on the MAIN thread (tui.py:4254, 4284 - not @work): at ~400 B/s the cap fires roughly every 3 days and reads+rewrites ~10 MB synchronously, a one-off ~50-100 ms UI stall. The unresolved structural split of diagnostic vs archival output (maintainer's closing caveat) is a code-organisation issue, not a scaling one.

incidents.title: monitor_daemon.log grew to 238 MB; TUI log panels readlines() the whole file every 1 s (800 MB RSS)
incidents.problem: BaseDaemonLogger appended with no rotation (238 MB after ~6 months). DaemonPanel and TUILogPanel called readlines() on the entire file every second to keep the last 100 lines, spiking the TUI to ~800 MB RSS and burning CPU.
incidents.fix: daemon_logging.py:31 MAX_LOG_BYTES=20 MB, _maybe_rotate (75-84) renames to a single .1 backup on every write once exceeded; tail_file_lines (34-58) reads at most the final 256 KB; both panels (daemon_panel.py:49-66, tui_log_panel.py:69-83) use it from @work threads and resume from the returned offset, re-tailing after rotation shrinks the file.
