incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: disk <= 40 MB per daemon (live + .1), per-second panel read <= 256 KB and normally incremental. _maybe_rotate stats the file on every log write (cheap). Local: monitor_daemon.log 5.2 MB, .log.1 21 MB - rotation is active.

incidents.title: TUI 5 s stats sweep re-parsed every Claude session file for every agent (CPU pin ~68%)
incidents.problem: _update_stats_async (tui.py:604 every 5 s) called read_session_file_stats with no cache; one long-lived agent with 115 MB across 15 static session files cost ~356 ms of JSON per sweep and pinned a core. Driven by history size, not agent count. Also _read_recent_events slurped whole hook_events_*.jsonl via readlines().
incidents.fix: history_reader.py:929-987: module cache keyed by path, invalidated on mtime/size/since change, _SESSION_STATS_CACHE_MAX=512 with oldest-half eviction; byte-identical output, ~64x faster warm sweep. _read_recent_events now reads a bounded growing tail (hook_status_detector.py:487-538).
incidents.residual_risk: The cache only helps STATIC files. Any transcript that changed since the last sweep is re-parsed in full (history_reader.py:966-977: whole-file _parse_session_lines on mtime/size mismatch). An active agent's transcript changes every few seconds, so at T_TRANSCRIPT=200 MB one active agent costs ~2-4 s of json.loads per 5 s sweep (GIL-held, in a worker) -> a pinned core; 50 active agents with 20 MB transcripts -> 1 GB of JSONL per 5 s, far past the cliff (sweep can't finish; exclusive worker just runs back-to-back). Cliff: sum of actively-changing transcript bytes > ~250 MB. Cache capacity cliff: 512 entries vs N_AGENTS x owned ids (<=20 each, hook_handler.py:260) x subagent files (history_reader.py:1180 glob per sweep) -> >~25 agents with many /clear'd sessions thrash the cache and re-parse static files too. Needed fix that keeps 5 s freshness: incremental parse from the last byte offset (proposed in #295, declined).

incidents.title: Evidence: `overcode monitor` at 65.8% CPU and 871 MB RSS after 56 min (March 2026), not investigated then
incidents.problem: The ps output pasted in #349 shows the TUI process at 65.8% CPU (37 CPU-min in 56 min wall) and 871 MB RSS, and the daemon at 9.4%. The issue was about a false duplicate-daemon warning; the CPU/RSS numbers were not examined.
incidents.fix: #353 fixed only the duplicate detection (fcntl lock probing replaces pgrep). The CPU/RSS pattern matches what PR #467 diagnosed five months later (log readlines() -> RSS; static-transcript re-parse -> CPU).
incidents.residual_risk: Same residual as the PR #467 session-stats incident: static files are now cached, but changing transcripts are still re-parsed whole every 5 s (history_reader.py:966-977). The 110% / 15 h report that triggered this audit is consistent with one or more large, actively-written transcripts plus the 4 Hz JSON parse sites (#291 incident).

incidents.title: Audit: 27 deferred performance/algorithmic issues (AUDIT.md) - partially implemented
incidents.problem: AUDIT.md (git b092101, lines 465-560) deferred 27 items: 250 ms blanket capture of all panes (#122), O(N^2) column widths (#123), render-all-widgets (#124), 10 s session reload without mtime check (#125), ANSI strip per render (#126), sessions cache 1 s TTL vs 250 ms timer so cache unused (#127), terminated sessions never GC'd (#128), sister polling not scaling (#129), ungated tree metadata (#130), config load_config uncached (#47), presence CSV uncached (#11), get_descendants O(N^2) (#33), clear_old_history whole-file (#43), history CSV parsed every 1 s render (#157/#158), etc. 'Scaling cliff at 20+ sessions'.
incidents.fix: PR #418 did: config TTL+mtime cache (config.py:21-63), column-width dirty flag (tui.py:297, 1000-1014), presence mtime+size cache (presence_logger.py:395-449), terminated-session GC after 600 s (tui.py:393, 1884-1896), widget change tracking. PR #352 did #126/#130; a96ff0f did #122 (tui_logic.py:923-943 select_capture_sessions); #467 did #157; 9115368 superseded #43.
incidents.residual_risk: Not done: #127 - _get_cached_sessions (tui.py:1109-1120, TTL 1 s) exists but the 250 ms fast path bypasses it and calls session_manager.list_sessions() directly (tui.py:1371) = full json.load of sessions.json 4x/s; #125 - refresh_sessions (tui.py:897) does launcher.list_sessions() full load + terminated detection every 10 s with no mtime gate; #11 - presence cache avoids re-parse only while the file is unchanged, it still linearly scans the whole CSV on each change (presence_logger.py:432-442); #129 unchanged (tui.py:612-615); #33 _compute_subtree_costs (monitor_daemon.py:1496-1512) per loop, complexity not verified. Item #123/#124 verified done.

incidents.title: TUI responsiveness quick wins: precompiled regexes, 550->100 capture lines for non-focused, strip ANSI once, tree gating
incidents.problem: Every 250 ms tick captured 550 lines per widget and ran 3+ strip_ansi regex passes per widget; regexes compiled per call; compute_tree_metadata O(N x depth) even outside tree sort. Cliff ~20 sessions.
incidents.fix: STATUS_CAPTURE_LINES for non-focused agents in the TUI (tui.py:1425), precompiled patterns, single strip in extract_from_pane, compute_child_counts O(N) when not in tree mode.
incidents.residual_risk: TUI side is bounded and further reduced by a96ff0f (non-focused captured 1-in-4 ticks). The DAEMON side was never reduced: StatusDetectorDispatcher's detectors default to capture_lines=DEFAULT_CAPTURE_LINES=500 (status_constants.py:16, status_detector.py:61, hook_status_detector.py:455) and _detect_and_enrich (monitor_daemon.py:1373-1380) calls detect_status for EVERY session EVERY 2 s loop -> one `tmux capture-pane -S -500 -e` subprocess per agent (implementations.py:128-140; pane object cached 30 s so exactly 1 spawn). At N=50: 25 spawns/s and ~1-2.5 MB/s of escape-laden pane text decoded and regex-scanned; at N=200: 100 spawns/s (~0.5-1 core in fork/exec alone). Status detection needs ~10-20 lines (this PR's own rationale). Freshness need: daemon status can lag 2 s; fix is depth reduction / hook-state mtime gating, not a slower loop.
incidents.degradation_note: Non-focused agents lost scrollback depth in their cached pane text, which is not displayed (preview shows only the focused agent).

incidents.title: Daemon loop 10 s -> 2 s and TUI daemon-state reads 5 s -> 1 s: 5x multiplier on every per-loop cost
incidents.problem: End-to-end latency for daemon-enriched data was ~15 s. Fix chose to run the whole daemon tick 5x more often (INTERVAL_FAST=2, settings.py:156; calculate_interval always returns it, monitor_daemon.py:910-917) and the TUI daemon-status worker at 1 Hz (tui.py:605).
incidents.fix: Cadence increase plus single-pass read_session_file_stats (one JSONL pass instead of two). Reduced latency ~15 s -> ~3 s.
incidents.residual_risk: Every per-session cost in _tick (monitor_daemon.py:1101-1126) now runs every 2 s: N pane captures (500 lines), N status-history CSV rows, and per session in _detect_and_enrich (1403-1419) refresh_git_context -> get_session (json.load sessions.json) + update_stats (locked load+dump) + get_session (json.load) = >=3 full parses and 1 full rewrite of sessions.json per agent per loop. At N=50 with sessions.json ~275 KB (5.5 KB/entry measured locally): ~50x(3x3 ms + dump) ~ 0.6-0.8 s of a 2 s loop (~35% core) before captures. Cliff: when terminated-but-unarchived entries push sessions.json to a few MB (N_SESSIONS_TOTAL ~2000 -> ~11 MB, ~100 ms/parse) the loop needs ~20 s > interval, so every daemon-fed number lags and the TUI's LOCK_SH readers contend with 25 LOCK_EX writes/s. Freshness need: status 2 s is right; fix is batching writes per tick (#292) and mtime-gating reads, not a slower loop.

incidents.title: SessionManager read-modify-write of all of sessions.json per call; ~30-50 round-trips per daemon loop
incidents.problem: _load_state/_save_state/_atomic_update open, flock, read, json.loads, modify, json.dump, rename the whole sessions.json on every update_stats/update_session/refresh_git_context call. Proposed in-memory cache with per-tick batch flush. Closed: 'hasn't caused measurable problems'; suggested batching within _tick if it ever does.
incidents.fix: None.
incidents.residual_risk: Unchanged in current code: _locked_state (session_manager.py:545-575) does full load+dump under LOCK_EX; update_stats (971-976) is called unconditionally for every session every 2 s loop (monitor_daemon.py:1413-1416), plus refresh_git_context/get_session parses (1403-1419) and list_sessions per session in sync_session_id every 10 s (monitor_daemon.py:699-701). Cost per loop ~ N_AGENTS x 4 x size(sessions.json), where size grows with N_SESSIONS_TOTAL live entries (~5.5 KB each locally). Quantified in the PR #324 incident; cliff at sessions.json of a few MB. Mitigation that keeps freshness: accumulate per-tick updates and flush once (maintainer's own suggestion), or write only when a field changed (current_task rarely changes).

incidents.title: TUI still parses sessions.json and monitor_daemon_state.json every 250 ms (json scanstring top symbol)
incidents.problem: Proposal: TUI reads status from daemon state instead of re-detecting. #324 made non-focused agents use daemon current_status when fresh, but the fast path still loads both files each tick.
incidents.fix: Partial: non-focused status from daemon; a96ff0f later reduced captures to focused + 1-in-4 rotation.
incidents.residual_risk: _fetch_statuses_async (tui.py:1362, every 250 ms) calls session_manager.list_sessions() (1371 -> full json.load with LOCK_SH, session_manager.py:421-445, 840-845) and get_monitor_daemon_state (1391 -> json.load, monitor_daemon_state.py:288-306) with no mtime gate; the 1 Hz _fetch_daemon_status_async (tui.py:642-656) parses daemon state again and sessions.json twice (656, daemon_status_bar.py:98). Daemon state is ~3 KB/session (9.1 KB for 3 locally, includes standing_instructions/activity_summary strings): N=50 -> 150 KB x 5 parses/s ~ 15 ms/s; sessions.json 275 KB x 6/s ~ 25 ms/s -> ~4% core at reference, matching the 2026-09-20 sample where json scanstring topped the profile. Cliff: N_SESSIONS_TOTAL ~2000 live entries (~11 MB) -> 4 Hz x ~100 ms = 40%+ of a core in the worker (GIL) just parsing. Fix keeping 250 ms freshness: cache parsed result by (mtime, size) - daemon state changes only every 2 s so 7 of 8 reads would hit; sessions.json needs daemon-side write batching (#292) for the gate to be effective.

incidents.ref: issue #295 (closed via PR #324, incremental parsing declined)
incidents.title: History reader: no incremental parsing - transcripts and ~/.claude/history.jsonl re-parsed whole on every change
incidents.problem: Proposed tracking (path, size, byte offset) so stats sync is O(new bytes). Closed as 'complexity for marginal gain' after single-pass reading.
incidents.fix: Single-pass read only; later #467 added a static-file cache (mtime/size).
incidents.residual_risk: (1) Transcripts: any changed file is fully re-parsed (history_reader.py:966-977) - see PR #467 incident. (2) history.jsonl: HistoryFile._entries (history_reader.py:501-536) re-reads and json.loads EVERY line whenever mtime/size changed; the file is fleet-global and changes on every user prompt from any agent. The TUI 5 s sweep constructs a NEW HistoryFile() per sweep (tui.py:1554) so its cache is always cold -> full parse every 5 s regardless. Locally 3.4 MB / 8,500 lines; at the colleague's 100,000 turns (~40 MB) that is ~0.4-0.8 s of JSON per sweep (~10-15% core) plus get_interactions_for_session (543-575) scanning all entries once per agent: 50 x 100k = 5M comparisons per sweep -> ~2-3 s per 5 s sweep. Cliff: ~50k history lines with 50 agents. Fix keeping 5 s freshness: module-level HistoryFile with byte-offset incremental append parsing and a per-session index.

incidents.title: Claude backend compute_window_burn re-parses every owned transcript at 1 Hz with no cache when baseline_minutes > 0
incidents.problem: DaemonStatusBar.fetch_volatile_state (daemon_status_bar.py:95-104), run by the 1 s worker (tui.py:605), calls compute_window_burn (tui_logic.py:533-571) for all non-asleep sessions; for Claude agents get_session_window_token_usage (history_reader.py:1290-1330) opens and json.loads every line of every owned session file (up to 20 per agent) via read_window_token_usage (1228-1290) - no mtime/size cache, unlike read_session_file_stats. Design doc: 'same 1 Hz cadence with no cache. It has not been reported as a problem.'
incidents.fix: None (opencode side was fixed in c6980b8; Claude path untouched).
incidents.residual_risk: Only active when the user cycles `,`/`.` to a non-zero spin baseline (persisted preference, tui.py:380). Then every second the worker requests a full parse of sum(owned transcript bytes): one 200 MB transcript = 2-4 s per call, so the exclusive 'daemon_status' worker runs back-to-back and pins a core indefinitely; 50 agents x 20 MB = 1 GB/s requested. Cliff: total active transcript bytes > ~50 MB. Fix keeping 1 s freshness: cache per (path, mtime, size, since-bucket) plus incremental tail parse, or have the daemon publish window totals it already computes at 60 s and interpolate.

incidents.title: 3 s GUI freeze every 5 s: blocking I/O (pgrep, CSV parses, JSON reads, log tail) on the Textual main loop
incidents.problem: update_daemon_status ran subprocess pgrep every 5 s on the main thread (worst on corp endpoint-security hosts); DaemonStatusBar.render() parsed CSVs and PID files on every repaint; timeline CSVs, session JSON and log tailing also on the main loop.
incidents.fix: All moved to @work(thread=True) workers with call_from_thread apply: refresh_sessions -> _fetch_sessions_async (tui.py:894), update_daemon_status -> _fetch_daemon_status_async (632-680), timeline fetch/apply split, panel tails in workers; render() reads cached instance vars only.
incidents.residual_risk: Main-thread I/O is essentially gone (remaining: _flush_heartbeat/_flush_status_changes appends + cap at tui.py:4254-4302 every 5 s; write_tui_heartbeat on keypress throttled 5 s). But the freeze mechanism was only moved, not bounded: CPython workers doing json.loads / JSONL parsing hold the GIL, so the input loop still stalls in proportion to parse volume - exactly what #476 reported ('GIL-holding work ... starve the UI's input loop'). The sites are the PR #467 transcript re-parse, the #291 4 Hz JSON parses, and the window-burn 1 Hz parse; their cliffs apply here as typing lag rather than a full freeze.

incidents.title: TUI CPU: libtmux spawned ~5 subprocesses per capture (~100 forks/s at 5 sessions); cache tmux objects, 250 -> 500 ms interval
incidents.problem: Each capture_pane did 5 subprocess calls; 5 sessions x 4 Hz = ~100 forks/s.
incidents.fix: RealTmux caches session/pane objects with _CACHE_TTL=30 s (implementations.py:30, 56-100) so a capture is one `tmux capture-pane` spawn; status interval raised to 500 ms (later restored to 250 ms, tui.py:601).
incidents.residual_risk: Per-capture cost is bounded (1 spawn), but spawn rate still scales with N_AGENTS: fast path captures focused + ceil(N/4) per 250 ms tick (tui_logic.py:920 NON_FOCUSED_CAPTURE_EVERY=4, 923-943) -> N=50: ~54 spawns/s; N=200: ~204 spawns/s (~1 core of fork/exec at 5 ms each) on top of the daemon's N/2 per s. Non-focused captures exist only to keep pane-derived columns fresh at ~1 Hz; the daemon already captures every pane every 2 s, so publishing the daemon's pane text (or a hash) would remove them without losing the 250 ms focused freshness. K_TMUX affects only list-windows calls (10 s refresh, 15 s resize, 5 s jobs) - bounded.
incidents.degradation_note: The 500 ms interval halved status/preview freshness; it was later reverted to 250 ms (#231 / tui.py:601), so no current degradation.

incidents.title: Preview pane on the 250 ms fast path; capture depth max(500, 2 x terminal height)
incidents.problem: Preview lagged 1-5 s (was on the 5 s path); capture depth hardcoded 50/200/500.
incidents.fix: _update_preview moved to _apply_status_results (copy of already-captured text, no I/O); detector.capture_lines = max(DEFAULT_CAPTURE_LINES=500, 2*height) on mount/resize (tui.py:884).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: focused capture is 1 spawn per 250 ms of <= max(500, 2h) lines with escape sequences (~150-300 KB at 300x100 -> ~1 MB/s through the pipe, strip_ansi + Rich from_ansi render). A 4K 200-row terminal still captures 500 lines. No growth with uptime.

incidents.title: Session-ID detection read all of history.jsonl (9.8 ms); now 64 KB reverse tail + mtime cache; daemon session-id sync every 10 s
incidents.problem: get_current_session_id_for_directory parsed the whole history.jsonl per call; daemon only found new ids on the 60 s stats cycle.
incidents.fix: _read_lines_reversed reads <= 64 KB from the end (history_reader.py:675-700) with mtime/size cache; daemon _sync_session_ids every 10 s (monitor_daemon.py:1224-1232); #373 added PID-based discovery + ownership guard; #412 added _discover_all_session_ids only when an agent has zero tokens (monitor_daemon.py:706-721).
incidents.residual_risk: Cost verified bounded: N x 64 KB per 10 s (N=50 -> 320 KB/10 s) plus is_session_id_owned_by_others over list_sessions() per session (O(N x N_SESSIONS_TOTAL) trivial, but each call re-parses sessions.json - counted in #292). Fidelity residual (not cost): with ~50 agents interleaving prompts into one history.jsonl (~400 B/line locally), 64 KB ~ 160 entries may not reach a given directory's latest entry, so post-/clear ids can be missed until the zero-token slow path or hook-reported ids catch up.

incidents.title: Keypress passthrough blocked the main loop 100-500 ms per key (send_keys_to_pane sleeps)
incidents.problem: _send_keys_to_focused called launcher.send_to_session_by_id synchronously; send_keys_to_pane sleeps 0.1-0.5 s between text and Enter; visible typing lag and chunky scroll.
incidents.fix: Fire-and-forget daemon thread per keypress, notify via call_from_thread (tui_actions/input.py:55-73).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: one short-lived thread per key, each <= 0.5 s, so concurrency <= typing rate x 0.5 (~5 threads at 10 keys/s); no queue or accumulation. Ordering relies on tmux serialising sends.

incidents.title: Compact mode: 15 s reconcile timer originally 1 + N tmux subprocess calls per tick
incidents.problem: Nested agent windows drift from the outer pane size; fix added a 15 s timer resizing every local window (1 + N spawns per 15 s; maintainer noted the churn).
incidents.fix: Merged; current code (tui.py:807-880) does one display-message + one list-windows per sweep and resize-window only for windows whose recorded size differs (tui_logic.py:946-960 windows_needing_resize), in an exclusive worker; only when self.compact.
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: steady state 2 spawns per 15 s regardless of N; N spawns only after a real size change. list-windows output scales with windows in the sync session (K_TMUX ~300 -> ~1 ms).

incidents.title: TUI interval timers never cancelled on unmount (claimed leak)
incidents.problem: 7+ set_interval timers in on_mount and DaemonPanel's 1 s timer are never stored/cancelled; feared runaway callbacks and worker leaks on remount.
incidents.fix: Won't fix: Textual cancels app-level timers on exit; widgets are not remounted.
incidents.residual_risk: Verified no growth: set_interval is only called in on_mount (tui.py:583-623), DaemonPanel.on_mount (daemon_panel.py:40) and TUILogPanel (tui_log_panel.py:60); DaemonPanel is composed once (tui.py:456). Widgets that are removed/mounted dynamically (SessionSummary rows, tui.py:2190-2248) own no timers. Timer count is constant for the process lifetime.

incidents.title: Timeline/status-history kept as CSV: in-memory window scales with N_AGENTS x hours; '24 h at 2 s is ~43K rows' was per-agent
incidents.problem: Proposal to move sessions/status/presence/daemon-state to SQLite. Closed: 'even 24h of history at 2s intervals is ~43K rows, trivially fast to scan' - that figure is for ONE agent; the daemon writes one row per agent per loop.
incidents.fix: None. StatusHistoryFile (status_history.py:59-235) gives mtime cache, binary seek to cutoff, and incremental tail reads.
incidents.residual_risk: Reads are incremental, but the cached window is materialised in the TUI process: rows = N_AGENTS x hours x 1800/h. At N=50 and the default 3 h timeline: ~270k 6-tuples (~80 MB RSS); with timeline.hours=24 or a 3 h spin baseline plus 24 h timeline: ~2.2M tuples (~650 MB). Every read runs a full list-comprehension _filter over the cached list (status_history.py:213-219) and _incremental_read re-filters it (138-140): the 30 s timeline plus the 1 Hz daemon-status worker when baseline_minutes > 0 (daemon_status_bar.py:78-85) -> 270k-2.2M tuple comparisons per second (~0.05-0.5 s of GIL per second). Cliff: N_AGENTS x window hours > ~500 agent-hours. Freshness need: timeline 30 s, spin 1 s - a ring buffer bucketed by slot width (timeline only draws `width` slots) would keep both at O(width).

incidents.title: Event bus instead of file polling declined; consumers poll monitor_daemon_state.json independently
incidents.problem: TUI, web server, supervisor each poll the daemon state file (~1-2 s) and diff it.
incidents.fix: None; #324's faster cadence deemed sufficient.
incidents.residual_risk: Per-consumer cost is the #291 incident (TUI 4 Hz + 1 Hz full parse). Total parse volume = consumers x rate x (~3 KB x N_AGENTS); with M_MULTI=5 TUIs on one host each parsing its own session's state it stays linear. Not a runaway by itself; the missing piece is an mtime gate on get_monitor_daemon_state (monitor_daemon_state.py:288-306) so a 2 s-cadence file is parsed at most once per change.

incidents.title: ~/.overcode/presence_log.csv has no rotation and is linearly re-scanned whole on every change (12 MB locally)
incidents.problem: PresenceLogger appends one row per DEFAULT_SAMPLE_INTERVAL=60 s (presence_logger.py:60, 264-311) forever; read_presence_history (401-449) runs csv.DictReader over the ENTIRE file from the top and keeps only rows within `hours`. #418 added an mtime+size cache, but the file changes every 60 s, so the timeline's 30 s refresh (status_timeline.py:91) re-scans the whole file every other tick; web_api.py:583/762 scan it per request.
incidents.fix: Cache only (no seek, no rotation).
incidents.residual_risk: Local 11.65 MB (~400k rows, ~9 months) -> ~0.5-1 s of DictReader per scan once a minute in the timeline worker (GIL-held burst -> a periodic stutter); grows ~15 MB/year with no cap. Cliff is gentle (linear), but it is unbounded and no issue tracks it. Fix keeping 30 s freshness: reuse StatusHistoryFile's binary _seek_to_cutoff + incremental tail (status_history.py:145-186), and rotate like agent_status_history.csv.

incidents.ref: src/overcode/hook_handler.py:333-389 (hook event log, added for #448; no tracking issue)
incidents.title: hook_events_<name>.jsonl rotation keeps 200 LINES but triggers on 100 KB: once lines average >512 B every hook event readlines() and rewrites the whole file
incidents.problem: append_hook_event writes the full tool_input per event (hook_handler.py:378-379, no truncation) then, if size > _EVENT_LOG_ROTATE_BYTES=100 KB (388-389), _rotate_event_log (337-352) reads ALL lines and rewrites the last 200. Edit/Write/MultiEdit inputs are KBs each, so 200 lines stay well over 100 KB and the rotation fires on EVERY subsequent event. Measured locally (read-only): hook_events_bobbit.jsonl = 1,426,096 B in exactly 200 lines (max line 9,012 B); miketap 367 KB / 200 lines with a 42,322 B line.
incidents.fix: None.
incidents.residual_risk: Per hook event on such an agent: read 1.4 MB + write 1.4 MB tmp + os.replace, inside Claude Code's synchronous hook path (adds ~5-15 ms latency to every tool call of that agent). Fleet: R_HOOKS=5/s -> ~14 MB/s of disk churn continuously. Grows with tool_input size (a 42 KB line means 200 lines ~ 8 MB rewritten per event). Detector only needs event, timestamp, tool_name (+ small fields), so truncating tool_input in the event log and rotating by byte size (keep the tail bytes) bounds it without any fidelity loss.

incidents.title: _read_recent_events re-reads a >=200 KB tail and JSON-parses 50 events on every detection of every idle agent, no cache
incidents.problem: HookStatusDetector.detect_status calls _most_recent_running_event_age whenever the hook event is Stop and status is waiting (hook_status_detector.py:691-696) - i.e. for every IDLE agent on every detection. _read_recent_events (487-538) reads a window of max(50*4096, 128 KB) = 200 KB, doubling until 50 lines are present (350 KB at the 7 KB/line seen locally -> 200 KB + 400 KB read), then json.loads the last 50 lines. #467 only bounded the read (was readlines() of the whole file).
incidents.fix: Bounded tail read; no mtime/size gating, no per-session parsed cache.
incidents.residual_risk: Detections per second: TUI (1 focused + ceil(N/4) rotating) x 4 Hz (tui.py:1362, tui_logic.py:920) + daemon N/2 (monitor_daemon.py:1380). N=50 all idle: ~54 + 25 = ~79 calls/s x (0.2-0.6 MB read + ~350 KB json) ~ 15-45 MB/s of reads and ~25 MB/s of json.loads across the two processes (~0.3-0.6 core, GIL-held in the TUI worker). Cliff: line sizes - a 42 KB line pushes the doubling loop toward reading the whole file each call. The log only changes on a hook event, so gating on (mtime, size) and caching the parsed 50 events per session keeps 250 ms fidelity at near-zero cost.

incidents.title: Monitor daemon always polls at the fast interval - idle backoff removed for data resolution
incidents.problem: Daemon dropped to 5 min / 1 h intervals when agents were idle, losing timeline granularity.
incidents.fix: calculate_interval always returns INTERVAL_FAST (monitor_daemon.py:910-917), now 2 s (settings.py:156).
incidents.residual_risk: By design the daemon does its full per-loop work (N captures at 500 lines, N CSV rows, ~4N sessions.json parses + N writes) every 2 s for 30 days even when every agent is idle or asleep (asleep sessions are still iterated; only 'done' skips capture, monitor_daemon.py:1376). Not growth, but it removes the natural idle bound and multiplies every other daemon site. Freshness need: 2 s for state changes; a hook-state mtime gate (skip capture when hook_state_<name>.json unchanged in hooks mode) would keep that and make idle cost ~0.

incidents.title: TUI keeps full polling cadence when the terminal is unfocused/backgrounded (no idle tier)
incidents.problem: Pane updates stopped when the macOS window lost focus; fix decoupled updates from Textual focus and kept 'tiered status updates that continue at 1 s in background'.
incidents.fix: Updates continue regardless of focus.
incidents.residual_risk: All timers (tui.py:583-623) run at full rate for the whole process lifetime; the 15 h x 110% report is the TUI doing its per-tick work while nobody is watching. Only the summarizer has an idle pause (tui.py:1939-1954). Freshness need while unfocused: none except stall notifications (already daemon-derivable) - a keypress/visibility-based tier that drops to daemon-state-only updates and resumes instantly on input would remove most idle cost without touching focused responsiveness.

incidents.title: Web /api/status captures 100 lines of EVERY agent's pane per request; each sister poll fans out N tmux spawns on the polled host
incidents.problem: get_status_data (web_api.py:108-141) calls _capture_agent_pane for every session in daemon state on every request; SisterPoller hits it every 10 s per sister (tui.py:612) plus a 1.5 s single-agent poll (tui.py:615, get_single_agent_status). #271 asked for per-request get_session_stats (declined as expensive; daemon state used instead - good).
incidents.fix: Stats come from daemon state (bounded); pane capture per request unchanged.
incidents.residual_risk: Polled host cost = (#pollers) x N_AGENTS spawns per 10 s: S=5 sisters polling a 50-agent host -> 25 spawns/s (~+1 daemon's worth); a 200-agent host with 2 pollers -> 40/s. Each RealTmux() is constructed per call (web_api.py:99) so the 30 s pane cache never warms - _get_pane costs an extra libtmux query per capture. The daemon already captures every pane every 2 s; serving its last capture (or a hash) from state would remove all per-request tmux work with <=2 s staleness, which matches the 10 s poll.

incidents.title: Nested tmux scroll jitter with dense ANSI output (visual diffs) in `overcode tmux` split layout
incidents.problem: Inner tmux client re-renders into the outer pane's PTY; dense per-character styling (diff highlighting) makes each update multi-write and briefly shows earlier scrollback. Reduced by terminal-features sync and window-size smallest, not eliminated. Worse at wider terminals.
incidents.fix: None (open; mitigations only).
incidents.residual_risk: Not a CPU/memory growth site in the two Python processes - the cost is tmux-side rendering proportional to bytes per update x terminal width. Listed for completeness as the only open performance/responsiveness issue.

incidents.title: Agent auto-sleep: idle claude processes not shut down to save RAM/CPU
incidents.problem: Idle agents with no background work keep a full claude process resident; proposal to sleep/wake them transparently. Closed with no comment or commit.
incidents.fix: None.
incidents.residual_risk: Outside the two monitored processes (it is the agents' own RSS/CPU), but it sets the fleet's baseline: N_AGENTS idle claude processes plus the daemon's per-agent work for each (see PR #29 incident). No overcode-side growth.

incidents.title: Verified bounded: done-check per refresh, untracked-window count, jobs kill detection
incidents.problem: #263: child stopped->done lagged 30 s; #344: unmanaged tmux windows suspected of sluggishness; #396: jobs falsely marked killed when list_windows returned [].
incidents.fix: #263: Stop hook + done-check on every TUI refresh (launcher.list_sessions -> _check_hook_stop/_check_report per session, launcher.py:938-941, every 10 s). #344 (aa95cd3): daemon counts untracked windows every 60 loops = 120 s (monitor_daemon.py:1545-1548), one list_windows. #396 (3aa23ae): skip kill detection on empty list + 30 s grace (job_launcher.py:109-135), driven by the 5 s _refresh_jobs timer (tui.py:617).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: N small hook_state reads per 10 s; one list-windows per 120 s (K_TMUX ~300 -> ~1 ms); one jobs.json read + one list-windows per 5 s (J_JOBS=50 trivial). launcher.list_sessions itself uses a single _list_tmux_windows_cheap call (launcher.py:927-931, from a96ff0f). jobs.json growth with completed jobs not checked.

incidents.title: read_presence_history full-file CSV re-parse; presence_log.csv never rotated
incidents.problem: read_presence_history parsed the entire presence_log.csv into memory on every call with no caching; the file is append-only and never pruned.
incidents.fix: An mtime+size+hours cache was added (src/overcode/presence_logger.py:395-450). No rotation/retention was added.
incidents.residual_risk: The cache is invalidated by every append, and PresenceLogger._run appends one row every PRESENCE.sample_interval=60 s (presence_logger.py:262-336; settings.py:180). The timeline worker (tui.py:607 set_interval(30) -> _fetch_timeline_async tui.py:733-765 -> status_timeline.py:91) therefore does a full csv.DictReader + datetime.fromisoformat pass over the whole file roughly once a minute, keeping only the last 3 h. No rotation exists anywhere in presence_logger.py (grep: no rotate/max/retention). Local file is 12 MB (~200k rows) -> ~0.5 s parse per minute in the timeline worker (~1% of a core). Growth rate is only ~100 KB/day at 60 s sampling, so 30 days ~3 MB; the cliff (>1 s per parse, timeline worker overlapping its 30 s period) is ~100 MB, i.e. years at the default interval or much sooner if sample_interval is lowered. Fix that keeps the 30 s timeline freshness: seek from the end to the 3 h cutoff exactly as StatusHistoryFile._seek_to_cutoff does (status_history.py:145-190), and/or rotate like agent_status_history.

incidents.title: get_descendants O(N^2) I/O; get_children full sessions.json parse is on the daemon hot loop
incidents.problem: get_descendants BFS calls get_children per node, each of which loads all sessions from disk, so descendant lookup is O(N^2) file I/O.
incidents.fix: Not fixed. get_descendants unchanged.
incidents.residual_risk: get_descendants (session_manager.py:1092-1100) -> get_children (1084-1090) -> list_sessions (840-845) -> _load_state json.load of the whole sessions.json per node. Its callers are launcher.py:1051, cli/budget.py:190, cli/agent.py:553 (user actions, not loops). The hot-loop problem is get_children itself: MonitorDaemon.track_session_stats calls session_manager.get_children(session.id) for every agent every tick (monitor_daemon.py:522, from _detect_and_enrich 1365-1494 at INTERVAL_FAST=2 s, settings.py:156) -> N full parses of sessions.json + N x N_SESSIONS_TOTAL Session.from_dict per tick. At 5.5 KB/entry (measured locally: 22 KB / 4 entries) the reference 50 agents / 200 entries (1.1 MB) costs ~50 x 10 ms + 10k from_dict = 0.6-0.8 s per 2 s tick from this call alone; at 200 agents / 2000 entries (11 MB) ~200 x 100 ms = 20 s per tick, so the daemon can never hold INTERVAL_FAST and every agent's daemon-sourced status goes stale. Fix with identical output: the tick already holds the full sessions list (monitor_daemon.py:1109); build a parent->child-count map once per tick and pass it into track_session_stats; give get_descendants a one-shot parent index.

incidents.ref: AUDIT.md #43 (also ux-perf §3 'clear_old_history is never called'; release notes 0.5.1 #465/#468, 0.5.3 'History rotation streams')
incidents.title: clear_old_history materialises the whole history CSV -- now dead code; streaming rotation is the live path
incidents.problem: clear_old_history read the entire agent_status_history.csv into memory, filtered and rewrote it; it was also never called, so the file grew without bound (2.4 GB / 21M rows reported in #468).
incidents.fix: Rotation/compression/retention added in 0.5.1 (#465/#468) and made streaming in 0.5.3: rotate_status_history (status_history.py:384-493) streams rows to two temp files, called hourly from the daemon via rotate_and_retain (monitor_daemon.py:1125, 1128-1157; interval 3600 s at 346). clear_old_history still exists (status_history.py:276-330) but has no callers.
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: rotation is a stat-gated hourly streaming pass (status_history.py:414-425 size/age trigger; docstring 400-412 states nothing is held in memory). Cost profile at reference: the daemon appends one row per agent per tick unconditionally (monitor_daemon.py:1461-1466), i.e. 25 rows/s at 50 agents (~2 KB/s, ~170 MB/day). ROTATION_KEEP_HOURS keeps >=30 h in the active file (status_history.py:336-345), so the active file floor is ~215 MB at 50 agents and ~860 MB at 200, and each hourly rotation streams+gzips that (~5-20 s CPU/hour in the daemon). Retention 540 days of ~25 MB/day gz archives ~13 GB at 50 agents. clear_old_history is dead code and can be deleted. The TUI-side cost of reading a 3 h window of this file is covered under AUDIT #157.

incidents.title: load_config re-read YAML on every get_* call
incidents.problem: Every config getter did file I/O + YAML parse.
incidents.fix: TTL (5 s) + mtime cache added: config.py:20-24 constants, load_config 45-75 (returns cached within TTL; after TTL a stat and re-parse only on mtime change), save_config invalidates (37-42).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: at most one stat per 5 s per process and a parse only when the file changed. Hot callers (get_user_config in compute_window_burn tui_logic.py:575 and sync_agent_stats monitor_daemon.py:840; get_history_retention_config hourly) are all served from cache.
incidents.degradation_note: Config edits become visible within 5 s instead of immediately; irrelevant to the monitored numbers.

incidents.title: start_web_server blocking time.sleep poll loop
incidents.problem: start_web_server spins 10 x 0.1 s time.sleep checking is_web_server_running.
incidents.fix: Not changed (web_server.py:576-586).
incidents.residual_risk: Still present but user-triggered once (start web server action), bounded at <=1 s. Not a scaling site.

incidents.ref: AUDIT.md #122 (also ux-perf §1; release notes 0.5.4 / commit a96ff0f)
incidents.title: 250 ms blanket pane capture of every agent
incidents.problem: The 250 ms fast path captured every session's pane via a tmux subprocess each tick: O(N) spawns at 4 Hz (80 captures/s at 20 agents).
incidents.fix: a96ff0f: select_capture_sessions (tui_logic.py:920-943, called tui.py:1394-1397) captures the focused agent every tick, rotates the others through a 1-in-4 slot, and always captures agents the daemon is not reporting; non-focused statuses come from daemon state (tui.py:1440-1476). Non-focused captures use STATUS_CAPTURE_LINES=100 (+50) (tui.py:1425; status_detector.py:96).
incidents.residual_risk: Bounded per tick but still linear in N with a 1 Hz floor per agent: per second the TUI spawns ~4 + N `tmux capture-pane` subprocesses (each also strip_ansi + pattern scans, status_detector.py:143). Reference 50 agents: ~54 spawns/s at 5-8 ms each = 25-40% of a core in the TUI plus tmux-server time, on top of the daemon's N/2 = 25 captures/s at 550 lines. At 200 agents: ~204 spawns/s (>1 core); the 8-thread pool (tui.py:1431) saturates and _status_update_in_progress (tui.py:1339-1341) drops ticks, so the focused agent's 250 ms target degrades to whatever N captures take. If the daemon is stale (>interval+5 s; tui.py:1387-1390) every agent is captured every tick: 4N/s. The tui.py:1330-1335 docstring ('updating all widgets is no more expensive than updating one') is stale. Fix that keeps 250 ms on the focused pane: when daemon state is fresh, have the daemon publish the pane-derived counts (extract_from_pane: background bash / live subagent) in its state so the TUI captures only the focused pane, or widen the rotation to 1-in-8/16 (those columns tolerate 2-5 s).
incidents.degradation_note: Non-focused pane-derived columns (bg bash count, subagent count, pane cache) lag up to 1 s instead of 250 ms -- documented in 0.5.4 notes and acceptable; status itself comes from the daemon at 2 s.

incidents.title: Column width recomputation every 250 ms
incidents.problem: Column contexts for all widgets were rebuilt and a width matrix computed every tick.
incidents.fix: Dirty-flag gating: _recompute_cell_column_widths (tui.py:986-1016) early-returns unless _column_widths_dirty (line 1000); dirty is set on structural changes (2111, 2180, 2256, 3720) and every stats sweep that changed any widget (1922-1924).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded and O(N x C) not O(N^2): when dirty, every widget's _build_column_context + render_summary_cells (~45 columns) then compute_column_widths. In practice _apply_stats_results marks dirty every 5 s (claude_stats is non-None for every Claude agent), so cost is ~50 x 45 cell renders per 5 s (~10-20 ms) at 50 agents and ~80 ms per 5 s at 200. The 4 Hz call at tui.py:1862 is a no-op unless dirty.

incidents.title: Widget refresh cascade: every SessionSummary refreshed every 250 ms regardless of change
incidents.problem: All widgets were refreshed after every status update even if nothing changed.
incidents.fix: Not fixed. apply_status_no_refresh returns a `changed` bool (session_summary.py:197-230) but the caller ignores it (tui.py:1838) and refreshes every widget (tui.py:1863-1864); _apply_daemon_status refreshes every widget again at 1 Hz (tui.py:721-724); _apply_summaries every 5 s (1990-1997).
incidents.residual_risk: Textual only re-renders widgets whose region intersects the viewport, so per-tick render work is ~min(N, visible rows) x SessionSummary.render (session_summary.py:470-495: get_terminal_size ioctl + _build_column_context + ~45 render functions + pad_and_join, ~0.5-1 ms each). On a 100-row terminal with >=100 agents that is ~100 renders x 4 Hz (+1 Hz) = 0.25-0.5 s/s of main-thread CPU (25-50% of a core) and visible keystroke latency, independent of N once N exceeds the viewport. Fix keeping 250 ms freshness: refresh only widgets whose apply_status_no_refresh returned True (or whose daemon-sourced status/activity changed), and cache the rendered Text keyed on the context tuple.

incidents.title: Session list reload every 10 s does a full JSON load + sort without an mtime check
incidents.problem: refresh_sessions reloads and re-sorts all sessions from disk every 10 s even when nothing changed.
incidents.fix: Not fixed; a96ff0f only reduced the tmux side (launcher.list_sessions uses one list-windows call, launcher.py:927-931).
incidents.residual_risk: refresh_sessions (tui.py:599 set_interval(10), 886-897) -> launcher.list_sessions (launcher.py:910-1000) -> SessionManager.list_sessions -> _load_state json.load under LOCK_SH + Session.from_dict for every entry including terminated ones (session_manager.py:421-470, 840-845; entries only leave sessions.json via delete_session 853). At 10 s this is minor (1 parse/10 s) -- the same parse at 4 Hz on the fast path is the real cost (see AUDIT #127). One fix bounds all callers with identical freshness: an (mtime, size)-keyed parse cache inside _load_state, since every writer bumps both.

incidents.title: ANSI stripping repeated per render cycle
incidents.problem: Pane content was regex-stripped on capture, again on render, again for status detection (~2000 regex ops/s at 10 sessions).
incidents.fix: Partially: the polling detector strips once per capture and passes clean_content down (status_detector.py:143; status_patterns.py:635, 852, 872 accept pre-cleaned text); SessionSummary.render no longer strips (session_summary.py:470-495 works from column context).
incidents.residual_risk: Two remaining sites. (a) Hooks mode strips the same pane up to three times per detect (hook_status_detector.py:72 dead-shell check, 92 interrupt check, 761 enrichment) for every captured agent in both the TUI and the daemon -- ~3 x 150-550 lines per capture, so ~3x the necessary regex work at N captures/s. (b) The preview pane rebuilds its Rich Text for the focused agent every 250 ms unconditionally: _apply_status_results tui.py:1871-1872 -> _update_preview 2971-2989 -> PreviewPane.update_from_widget preview_pane.py:76-96 -> _build_content runs four regex subs (_sanitize_ansi, lines 33-38) plus Text.from_ansi per line over max(500, 2 x terminal height)+50 lines (tui.py:881-884; status_detector.py:96) = ~2000-2400 lines/s x 5 ops on the main thread, ~10-30 ms per tick (5-10% of a core) for a single agent, scaling with V_TERM. Fix keeping 250 ms: skip the rebuild when widget.pane_content is unchanged (identity/hash compare); strip once in the hooks detector and reuse.

incidents.ref: AUDIT.md #127 (also 2026-09-20 native CPU sample: json scanstring top symbol)
incidents.title: TUI sessions cache (1 s TTL) is unused; sessions.json is fully re-parsed ~6x per second
incidents.problem: The session cache had a 1 s TTL while the timer fired every 250 ms, so it was effectively unused.
incidents.fix: Not fixed -- now literally unused: _get_cached_sessions (tui.py:1110-1121) has zero callers (grep). Every worker calls session_manager.list_sessions() directly.
incidents.residual_risk: Parse rate of sessions.json in the TUI: _fetch_statuses_async 4 Hz (tui.py:601 -> 1362-1370), _fetch_daemon_status_async 1 Hz (tui.py:605 -> 655) plus daemon_status_bar.fetch_volatile_state again at 1 Hz when baseline_minutes>0 (daemon_status_bar.py:97-101), _update_stats_async 0.2 Hz (1543), _update_summaries_async 0.2 Hz (1973), refresh_sessions 0.1 Hz -- about 5.5-6.5 full json.load + Session.from_dict passes per second, each under flock LOCK_SH (session_manager.py:434-440). At the measured 5.5 KB/entry (indent=2, duplicate legacy keys): 200 entries (1.1 MB) costs ~60-70 ms/s (6% of a core); 2000 entries (11 MB) ~0.6-0.7 s/s -- a full core in json scanstring, matching the 2026-09-20 sample. Cliff ~2 MB (~350 entries). Each LOCK_SH also serialises against the daemon's N-per-tick LOCK_EX read-modify-writes (see ux-perf §4 incident). Fix keeping 250 ms freshness: (mtime, size)-gated cache in SessionManager._load_state (writers bump both), so parses drop to the file's write rate.

incidents.title: Terminated sessions never garbage-collected in the TUI
incidents.problem: _terminated_sessions accumulated Session objects forever with TUI uptime.
incidents.fix: _gc_terminated_sessions (tui.py:1884-1896) with _TERMINATED_GC_SECONDS=600 (tui.py:391-393), called from _apply_stats_results every 5 s (tui.py:1900); entries also removed on revive/archive (3605-3609, 3676-3677).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: at most the sessions terminated in the last 10 minutes are held.

incidents.title: Sister polling is sequential with per-sister timeouts and does not scale with sister count
incidents.problem: Sister polls run one at a time; unreachable sisters stall the whole poll.
incidents.fix: Not fixed: poll_all is sequential (sister_poller.py:74-80) with a 5 s urlopen timeout per sister (180); poll_all_timelines is sequential inside the 30 s timeline worker (126-137, timeout 5 s at 152).
incidents.residual_risk: With S unreachable sisters each 10 s poll (tui.py:612 -> 1623-1631) takes 5S s (25 s at S=5); exclusive thread workers cannot be cancelled so up to ceil(5S/10) workers overlap (bounded, ~3 threads) but the remote agent list lags 25 s+ and the timeline worker (which also does the local CSV reads) is blocked 25 s of every 30 s. Payload: every /api/status response embeds 100 lines of pane content for every remote agent (web_api.py:100, 119-124) ~10 KB/agent -> ~500 KB per sister per 10 s at 50 remote agents (~5 ms JSON parse). Freshness needed: remote list <=10 s, focused remote agent 1.5 s (already a separate poll, tui.py:1657-1680). Fix keeping cadence: ThreadPoolExecutor across sisters, shorter connect timeout, and make pane_content optional on the list endpoint.

incidents.title: Tree metadata recomputed even when tree sort disabled
incidents.problem: compute_tree_metadata ran O(N x depth) on every widget update regardless of sort mode.
incidents.fix: Gated: tui.py:2391-2400 runs compute_tree_metadata only when sort_mode == 'by_tree', otherwise compute_child_counts (O(N)).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: runs inside update_session_widgets (10 s refresh / structural changes), O(N) in non-tree mode and O(N x depth) only in tree mode.

incidents.title: time.sleep(1.0) blocks the Textual event loop while starting the Monitor Daemon
incidents.problem: Blocking sleep on the main thread during supervisor start.
incidents.fix: Not fixed: tui_actions/daemon.py:64 time.sleep(1.0) inside _do_supervisor_start.
incidents.residual_risk: User-triggered once; freezes the UI for 1 s. Not a scaling site; should be set_timer(1.0, ...).

incidents.ref: AUDIT.md #157 (also ux-perf §8; daemon_status_bar.py:77 comment 'expensive CSV parse')
incidents.title: Status bar parses agent_status_history.csv every 1 s when a baseline window is set
incidents.problem: DaemonStatusBar re-parsed the history CSV on every 1 s render cycle when baseline_minutes > 0.
incidents.fix: Parse moved off the main thread and made incremental: read_agent_status_history -> module-level StatusHistoryFile with mtime+size cache, binary-search seek to cutoff, and append-only incremental reads (status_history.py:59-142, 145-190, 220-256).
incidents.residual_risk: The parse is bounded (only new bytes per second) but every 1 Hz call still does three O(window rows) passes: _incremental_read trims the cached list (status_history.py:136-137), _filter list-comprehends the whole cache (213-217), and calculate_mean_spin_from_history scans it again with `agent in agent_names` list membership (tui_logic.py:477-487). The reader is shared with the 30 s timeline read (status_timeline.py:95 asks 3 h), so after the first timeline read the cache holds 3 h regardless of baseline: rows = N_AGENTS x 10800 / INTERVAL_FAST(2) = 270k tuples at 50 agents (~60 MB of Python objects resident in the TUI), ~100-200 ms/s of CPU in the daemon_status worker (10-20% of a core); at 200 agents ~1.1M rows and ~0.5-0.8 s/s so the exclusive 1 Hz worker (tui.py:633) overruns and uncancellable threads pile up. Only active when baseline_minutes > 0 (daemon_status_bar.py:78). Cliff ~500k window rows. Fix keeping 1 Hz: maintain running per-agent green/total counters over a timestamp deque fed by the incremental rows; make agent_names a set; or reduce row volume at the source (log status changes + periodic keepalive) since timeline slots are >=30 s.

incidents.title: History CSV parsed three times per interval by different call sites
incidents.problem: tui.py, daemon_status_bar.py and the timeline each parsed the same CSV independently.
incidents.fix: Module-level shared reader: _get_or_create_reader keyed by path (status_history.py:220-234); status bar (daemon_status_bar.py:79-82) and timeline (status_timeline.py:95) reuse one parsed cache.
incidents.residual_risk: Verified: one parse per file change shared by all callers. The per-call O(window) filtering cost that remains is reported under AUDIT #157.

incidents.title: shutil.get_terminal_size() on every SessionSummary render
incidents.problem: Terminal size queried per render instead of per resize.
incidents.fix: Not fixed (session_summary.py:471-473).
incidents.residual_risk: One ioctl (~3 us) per render; at <=400 visible renders/s that is ~1 ms/s. Negligible; self.app.size is already available.

incidents.title: Reactive watchers fire redundant refreshes
incidents.problem: Reactive attribute watchers triggered refresh even when values were unchanged.
incidents.fix: No code change needed: Textual reactives skip watchers when the value is unchanged by default; watch_summary_detail / watch_summary_content_mode (session_summary.py:292-298) only fire on real user toggles.
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: a detail-level toggle fires N refreshes once per keypress.

incidents.title: shutil.get_terminal_size() per timeline_width access
incidents.problem: Same as #159 in StatusTimeline.
incidents.fix: Not fixed (status_timeline.py:63-79).
incidents.residual_risk: Called during timeline renders (30 s cadence plus resize). Negligible.

incidents.title: _col_effective linear scan over SUMMARY_COLUMNS
incidents.problem: O(C) scan per lookup instead of dict.
incidents.fix: Not fixed (summary_config_modal.py:96-108).
incidents.residual_risk: C ~45 columns; modal-only. Negligible.

incidents.title: Linear column scan per row per render in the summary config modal
incidents.problem: Same scan inside the render loop.
incidents.fix: Not fixed (summary_config_modal.py:155, 299).
incidents.residual_risk: ~45 x rows comparisons per modal render (~2k). Negligible; modal only.

incidents.title: render_status_plain reverse-looks-up the status name from its symbol
incidents.problem: O(|ALL_STATUSES|) reverse lookup with get_status_symbol per candidate on every render.
incidents.fix: Not fixed (summary_columns.py:1095-1104).
incidents.residual_risk: <=12 lookups per widget render on the plain-render path (registered at summary_columns.py:1320). Negligible.

incidents.title: /api/status captures every agent's pane with a fresh RealTmux per agent; single-threaded HTTPServer, no ETag/gzip
incidents.problem: get_status_data created a StatusDetector per call; the web API returned full state incl. pane content for all agents on every poll, sequentially, from a single-threaded server.
incidents.fix: The StatusDetector instantiation is gone; the shape of the cost moved: get_status_data (web_api.py:107-143) reads daemon state and calls _capture_agent_pane for every session (119-124), which constructs a new RealTmux() per agent (98-99) and captures 100 lines. Server is still stdlib HTTPServer (web_server.py:12, 417); no ETag or Content-Encoding anywhere (grep).
incidents.residual_risk: A fresh RealTmux per agent defeats its 30 s pane cache (implementations.py:31-42), so each capture is preceded by libtmux server/session/window lookups: roughly 3-4 subprocesses per agent per request. Callers that make this a long-lived-process load: every sister TUI polls /api/status every 10 s (sister_poller.py:172-185) and the daemon's relay push calls get_status_data every 30 s when relay is configured (monitor_daemon.py:1040-1063). At 50 agents and one sister: ~200 tmux commands per 10 s on the tmux server; M sisters multiply it. Cliff ~500 commands/10 s (typing lag on the host). Freshness needed: remote list 10 s; only the focused remote agent needs pane content at 1.5 s and already has its own endpoint. Fix: make pane_content opt-in (?include_pane=), reuse one RealTmux, ThreadingHTTPServer.

incidents.title: update_summaries iterates sessions multiple times
incidents.problem: Six generator passes over self.sessions instead of one.
incidents.fix: Not fixed (monitor_daemon_state.py:237-244).
incidents.residual_risk: Runs once per save, i.e. once per daemon tick (save at 260-286 called from monitor_daemon.py:1035). 6N per 2 s: microseconds. Negligible.

incidents.title: OvercodeHandler.tmux_session class variable mutated externally
incidents.problem: Global mutable state on the handler class.
incidents.fix: Not fixed (web_server.py:133, 412; web_server_runner.py:80).
incidents.residual_risk: Not a performance item.

incidents.title: YAML config not schema-validated
incidents.problem: Unknown keys silently accepted.
incidents.fix: Not fixed (no validation in config.py; grep 'validate' finds nothing).
incidents.residual_risk: Not a performance item.

incidents.title: Data file growth: status history rows written per tick, archive.json and agent_session_ids uncapped
incidents.problem: agent_status_history.csv, presence_log.csv, archive.json and claude_session_ids grew without pruning; clear_old_history never called.
incidents.fix: agent_status_history.csv: hourly streaming rotation + 540-day retention (status_history.py:384-546; monitor_daemon.py:1128-1157). presence_log: caching only (see AUDIT #11). archive.json and agent_session_ids: unchanged.
incidents.residual_risk: (a) Row volume is the driver: log_agent_status is called for every agent every tick even when status is unchanged (monitor_daemon.py:1461-1466) -> N/INTERVAL_FAST rows/s = 25 rows/s at 50 agents (~170 MB/day raw, active file >=30 h ~215 MB, TUI 3 h window 270k rows). Writing only on status change plus a 30 s keepalive would cut this 10-50x with no loss for the timeline (30 s slots) -- mean-spin would need change-aware weighting. (b) archive.json: every deleted session is appended forever (session_manager.py:853-914; 3.4 KB/entry, 320 entries = 1.1 MB locally) but it is loaded only by archive/restore operations (917-942), never in the TUI/daemon loops -> bounded for the long-lived processes. (c) agent_session_ids: appended on every /clear with no cap and written under both canonical and legacy keys (session_manager.py:1046-1056; 19 ids live / 58 archived locally); get_session_window_token_usage stats and globs a subagents dir per id per second when baseline>0 (history_reader.py:1318-1345) -> ~2 x ids syscalls/s/agent, minor. (d) clear_old_history is still never called but superseded by rotation.

incidents.ref: docs/ux-performance-analysis-2026-03-09.md §4 (full JSON state rewrite per daemon cycle; per-session writes)
incidents.title: Daemon does 3 full loads + 1 fsync'd full rewrite of sessions.json per agent per tick
incidents.problem: monitor_daemon_state.json rewritten every cycle; multiple session updates within a cycle each triggered separate writes.
incidents.fix: monitor_daemon_state.json is written once per tick (MonitorDaemonState.save monitor_daemon_state.py:260-286 from _publish_state monitor_daemon.py:1004-1035; plus wake at 933) -- bounded (~150 KB indent=2 + fsync at 50 agents, ~3-5 ms). The per-session sessions.json traffic was not addressed.
incidents.residual_risk: Per agent per tick in _detect_and_enrich: refresh_git_context -> get_session full json.load (session_manager.py:718-741, 825-830); update_stats(current_task=...) unconditionally even when unchanged (monitor_daemon.py:1409-1412) -> _locked_state LOCK_EX + json.loads + json.dump(indent=2) + fsync of the whole file (session_manager.py:971-977, 544-597); get_session again (monitor_daemon.py:1415); get_children (522) another full load. Plus _sync_process_resources every 5 s writes update_session per agent whose CPU moved >=1% (monitor_daemon.py:1300-1310) -- true for most busy agents. Reference 50 agents with a 1.1 MB sessions.json (200 entries): ~150 loads x 10 ms + 50 dumps x 15 ms + 50 fsyncs x 3-10 ms = 2.5-3 s per 2 s tick -> the daemon cannot hold INTERVAL_FAST; at the local 4-agent/22 KB file it is ~12 x 0.3 ms and invisible. Cliff ~ N_AGENTS x file_MB >= ~20 (e.g. 20 agents x 1 MB). The 50 LOCK_EX windows per tick also block the TUI's 4-6 Hz LOCK_SH reads. Fix with identical published output: pass the already-loaded Session into refresh_git_context/track_session_stats, write current_task only on change, and coalesce all per-tick session updates into one _locked_state write.

incidents.title: Regex patterns compiled per call in status detection
incidents.problem: _is_shell_prompt / _matches_approval_patterns compiled patterns on every call.
incidents.fix: Pre-compiled: module-level patterns (status_detector.py:39), per-instance compiled approval/error patterns (78-84), StatusPatterns compiles regex fields once (status_patterns.py:318).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded.

incidents.title: Daemon still captures 550 lines per agent per tick for status detection
incidents.problem: Status detection captured 550 lines when the last ~10 suffice.
incidents.fix: TUI only: non-focused agents capture STATUS_CAPTURE_LINES=100 (+50) (tui.py:1425; status_constants.py:17); focused captures max(500, 2 x height)+50 (tui.py:881-884). The daemon calls detector.detect_status(session) with no num_lines (monitor_daemon.py:1380) so it uses DEFAULT_CAPTURE_LINES=500 (+50) (status_detector.py:61, 96; status_constants.py:16) for every agent every tick, in both polling and hooks modes (hook_status_detector.py:648, 653, 583-587).
incidents.residual_risk: Per tick at 50 agents: 50 x 550 lines (~2.75 MB) piped from tmux, strip_ansi'd and scanned line-by-line by the pattern functions -> ~50-100 ms CPU per 2 s tick plus tmux-server time; 200 agents ~11 MB per tick. Status uses the last few lines; extract_pr_number (monitor_daemon.py:1392-1395) scans the whole capture. Fix: daemon passes num_lines=STATUS_CAPTURE_LINES -- identical status fidelity (the TUI already accepts this for non-focused agents); PR URLs printed >100 lines back could be missed.

incidents.title: tmux -V / <agent> --version subprocess on every Launcher construction
incidents.problem: 50-100 ms of version subprocesses per CLI invocation.
incidents.fix: Not cached (dependency_check.py:59-89) but only reached via Launcher init (launcher.py:40 imports require_tmux/require_agent_cli); the hook-handler fast path (a96ff0f) bypasses the CLI entirely.
incidents.residual_risk: CLI/TUI-startup cost only; not on any loop of the two long-lived processes.

incidents.title: Claude settings JSON read-modify-write per add_hook/remove_hook
incidents.problem: Installing 5 hooks did 5 separate load/save cycles.
incidents.fix: Not changed (claude_config.py:57-95 _modify_settings per call).
incidents.residual_risk: Install-time only; not a runtime scaling site.

incidents.title: Web API responses uncompressed
incidents.problem: Large JSON responses sent without gzip.
incidents.fix: Not changed (no Content-Encoding in web_server.py).
incidents.residual_risk: Affects sister polling bandwidth only (~500 KB per sister per 10 s at 50 remote agents with pane content). Low.

incidents.title: Hooks mode is authoritative for status but the daemon and TUI still capture every pane every period
incidents.problem: Daemon polls tmux for idle sessions; no kqueue/inotify on hook state files.
incidents.fix: Not implemented. Hook state is the sole authority with no polling fallback (hook_status_detector.py:9, 435), but HookStatusDetector.detect_status still calls get_pane_content for every agent on every detect for enrichment/dead-shell/interrupt checks (hook_status_detector.py:617, 648-653) and reads hook_state JSON + a bounded tail of hook_events per agent (554-580, 487-530).
incidents.residual_risk: In hooks mode the tmux command rate is unchanged from polling mode: daemon N captures per 2 s, TUI ~4 + N captures/s (see AUDIT #122). Per-agent file reads are cheap and bounded (hook_state ~200 B; hook_events tail <=128 KB window). An mtime check on hook_state before capturing (skip the pane when neither the hook state nor the previous content hash changed) would cut most non-focused captures with no loss of status fidelity.

incidents.title: opencode/opencode2 stats readers: quadratic IN+ORDER BY+LIMIT scan and per-call body parsing
incidents.problem: get_stats/get_window_token_usage cost up to 115-254 ms per agent per call against a ~2 GB opencode.db; TUI calls once per second per agent (burn) and every 5 s (stats).
incidents.fix: Per-conversation bounded index-ordered probes selecting narrow columns, Python-side merge, and a module-level per-row parse cache keyed (store, table, row id) -> (time_updated, record), capped at 50,000 entries dropping the oldest half (opencode_stats.py ~334 area, opencode2_stats.py ~227 area). The proposed 60 s TTL cache was declined; TUI cadence unchanged.
incidents.residual_risk: Design doc reports 254 ms -> 9.6 ms (opencode2, 8 owned ids) on a 2.3 GB store; cache memory bounded at a few MB; in-flight rows never cached so streaming turns stay fresh. Not re-benchmarked in this pass. Same freshness (1 Hz / 5 s) retained. Doc's own open item: the Claude backend's equivalent 1 Hz path is uncached -- see next incident.

incidents.ref: docs/design/opencode-stats-reader-performance.md 'Open questions' (Claude read_window_token_usage re-parses JSONL at 1 Hz with no cache)
incidents.title: 1 Hz burn-rate path json.loads every line of every Claude transcript with no cache
incidents.problem: Documented as an open question: the Claude backend re-parses transcript JSONL at the same 1 Hz cadence the opencode fix addressed, with no cache. Not reported as a problem at the time.
incidents.fix: None.
incidents.residual_risk: Trigger chain: tui.py:605 set_interval(1, update_daemon_status) -> _fetch_daemon_status_async (633-680, exclusive thread worker) -> DaemonStatusBar.fetch_volatile_state (daemon_status_bar.py:62-118) -> compute_window_burn when baseline_minutes > 0 (93-102; tui_logic.py:533-600, docstring: 'cache externally if you have hundreds') -> ClaudeStatsReader.get_window_token_usage (stats_reader.py:186-190) -> get_session_window_token_usage (history_reader.py:1296-1345) -> read_window_token_usage (1228-1290): opens every owned session file and every subagent file and json.loads EVERY line, every second; nothing is cached and `since` changes each call so a memo would never hit. Reference T_TRANSCRIPT 200 MB / 5000 turns: json.loads at ~50-100 MB/s = 2-4 s per file per 1 s tick; 50 agents x 20 MB = 1 GB/s of parsing requested. The exclusive worker overruns, uncancellable threads pile up, and one core stays pinned indefinitely while the burn/mean-spin figures go stale -- the most plausible single explanation for '110% CPU for 15 hours' if the user had a baseline window selected. Cliff: sum of live transcript bytes >= ~30 MB. Fix that keeps 1 Hz and exact totals: per-file incremental reader holding (offset, mtime, size) and a deque of (timestamp, usage) for assistant messages; parse only appended bytes, evict entries older than `since`, sum the deque -> O(new bytes) per second.

incidents.ref: docs/design/opencode-stats-reader-performance.md 'Open questions' (TUI 5 s get_stats duplicates daemon 60 s sync); history_reader.py:923-928 comment ('re-parsed every static file every 5s, pinning a CPU core')
incidents.title: Active transcript and ~/.claude/history.jsonl fully re-parsed whenever they change (5 s TUI sweep, 60 s daemon sync)
incidents.problem: Both the TUI (5 s) and daemon (60 s) call get_stats for every agent; an earlier incident (documented in the history_reader.py comment) had every static session file re-parsed every 5 s.
incidents.fix: read_session_file_stats cache keyed (path, mtime, size, since), max 512 entries (history_reader.py:923-990); HistoryFile caches history.jsonl by mtime+size (479-535); a HistoryFile is shared per sweep (tui.py:1555).
incidents.residual_risk: Static files are now parsed once, but (a) the ACTIVE transcript changes on every turn/tool call, so each 5 s sweep (tui.py:604 -> 1527-1620, 8-thread exclusive slow_stats worker) and each 60 s daemon sync (monitor_daemon.py:1234-1242 -> 793-870) re-parses it in full via _parse_session_lines: a 200 MB active file costs 2-4 s per sweep, so >=2 such agents overrun the 5 s period and workers pile up; cliff ~50 MB active transcript. (b) HistoryFile._entries (history_reader.py:501-535) re-parses ALL of ~/.claude/history.jsonl whenever it changes, and it changes on every prompt of any Claude Code session machine-wide: at the measured ~400 B/line, 100k turns ~40 MB (~0.4-0.8 s per parse); with 50 agents prompting every ~30 s the file changes every 1-2 s, so effectively every 5 s TUI sweep and 60 s daemon sync pays it, and get_interactions_for_session then walks all entries per agent (N x 100k iterations per sweep; the no-owned-ids fallback branch does Path.resolve per entry). Cliff ~20 MB history.jsonl with a busy fleet. Fix keeping 5 s / 60 s freshness and exact numbers: append-only incremental parsing for both files (remember offset; keep running totals; current_context_tokens needs only the last assistant message, tail-readable). Also consider letting the TUI read the daemon's 60 s numbers for cost/token columns (5 s -> 60 s would be a fidelity trade; incremental parsing avoids it).

incidents.ref: docs/release-notes-0.5.1.md (#465, #468 unbounded agent_status_history.csv and diagnostics/event_loop_timing.csv) + docs/release-notes-0.5.3.md ('History rotation streams')
incidents.title: History CSV rotation/retention and diagnostic CSV hard caps
incidents.problem: agent_status_history.csv (2.4 GB / 21M rows) and event_loop_timing.csv (3.7 GB) grew without rotation and filled a disk; the first rotation implementation loaded the whole file.
incidents.fix: Hourly rotation to .csv.gz when >50 MB or >7 days, 540-day retention, streaming implementation (status_history.py:384-546; monitor_daemon.py:1128-1157); windowed readers untouched (keep >=30 h). event_loop_timing.csv and status_changes.csv hard-capped at 100 MB per the notes.
incidents.residual_risk: Rotation verified streaming and stat-gated hourly (see AUDIT #43 incident). The diagnostic CSV cap enforcement was not re-read in this pass (TUI flush points at tui.py:4254-4262 and 4284-4300 swap the in-memory buffers every 5 s, so in-memory growth is bounded). No freshness traded: rotation never touches the most recent 30 h.

incidents.title: 0.5.4 tmux/subprocess load reductions: which ones traded freshness
incidents.problem: tmux typing lag from the number of tmux commands per second issued by the TUI and daemon.
incidents.fix: (1) hook-handler dispatched before CLI import (~20 ms vs 80 ms per hook event); (2) TUI captures focused agent at 4 Hz, others 1-in-4 (tui_logic.py:920-943); (3) resize sweep only resizes windows whose size changed (tui.py:821-879, windows_needing_resize tui_logic.py:946-960); (4) launcher.list_sessions one list-windows call (launcher.py:927-931); (5) git diff/untracked once per distinct directory every 3rd 5 s sweep (tui_logic.py:963-974; tui.py:1557-1580); (6) daemon reads .git/HEAD directly (session_manager.py:666-690).
incidents.residual_risk: (1),(3),(4),(6) trade nothing. (2) and (5) trade freshness (see note). Residual: (5) still spawns `git diff --stat` + untracked-count per distinct directory every 15 s, each walking the working tree (O(repo size)); (6) refresh_git_context still does a full sessions.json get_session per agent per tick (session_manager.py:727) -- the subprocess is gone but the JSON parse remains (ux-perf §4 incident); (2) remains linear in N (AUDIT #122 incident).
incidents.degradation_note: Non-focused pane-derived columns lag up to 1 s (was 250 ms) -- acceptable, status comes from the daemon at 2 s. Git diff/untracked columns lag up to 15 s (was 5 s) -- acceptable for those columns; the focused agent's diff could be kept at 5 s cheaply if wanted.

incidents.ref: docs/release-notes-0.4.2.md ('CPU and RAM columns, fed by a process-tree sampler'); process_resources.py:6 comment
incidents.title: Machine-wide `ps -eo` every 5 s plus per-agent pane-pid lookup
incidents.problem: Per-agent CPU/RSS columns require walking the process table.
incidents.fix: One batched `ps -eo pid,ppid,%cpu,rss,args` per 5 s (process_resources.py:29-60; interval monitor_daemon.py:341, gate 1261-1263) then BFS per agent tree; writes gated on >=1% CPU / 1 MiB RSS change (1300-1310).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: 1 ps (~10-30 ms for ~1000 processes; scales with machine process count, not an axis) + N tmux.get_pane_pid lookups per 5 s (monitor_daemon.py:1284; 10/s at 50 agents) + O(processes) BFS. The change-gated update_session writes feed the sessions.json rewrite problem (ux-perf §4 incident) but are otherwise bounded.

incidents.ref: hook_status_detector.py:487-497 docstring (#448 follow-up: 'multi-MB hook-event log ... was pinning a CPU core'); hook_handler.py:333-336 rotation
incidents.title: hook_events_<name>.jsonl read whole on every detection cycle
incidents.problem: The detector slurped the entire append-only hook event log per agent per detect; a long-lived agent's multi-MB log pinned a core.
incidents.fix: _read_recent_events reads a bounded tail (max(50 x 4 KB, 128 KB) window, doubling until 50 lines; hook_status_detector.py:487-530, _RECENT_EVENTS_LIMIT=50 at 147). Writer rotates at >100 KB keeping the last 200 lines (hook_handler.py:333-336, 338-357, 388-392).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: reads <=128 KB (or a few doublings for large tool_input payloads) per agent per detect; rotation readlines() at most ~100 KB per ~250 events. The local 1.4 MB hook_events_bobbit.jsonl (mtime 18 Aug) predates rotation and would cost only its tail. Per-event hook cost is O(1) plus one stat.

incidents.ref: docs/architecture.md 'What's Concerning' §4 (daemon coupling via shared files; TUI reads all four)
incidents.title: TUI polls four shared state files by full re-parse; aggregated parse budget
incidents.problem: The daemon, session manager, status history and presence logger each write a file the TUI re-reads; no schema/versioning, no change gating at read time.
incidents.fix: None at the loader level (history CSV has mtime+incremental cache; presence has mtime cache; sessions.json and monitor_daemon_state.json have none).
incidents.residual_risk: Per second in the TUI: sessions.json ~5.5-6.5 full parses (AUDIT #127 incident); monitor_daemon_state.json ~5-6 full parses -- fast path 4 Hz (tui.py:1386), daemon status 1 Hz (642), daemon_panel 1 Hz when open (daemon_panel.py:52), update_session_widgets every 10 s (2034) -- at ~3 KB/session (measured 9.1 KB / 3 sessions) that is 150 KB at 50 agents (~10 ms/s) and 600 KB at 200 (~40 ms/s) via MonitorDaemonState.load json.load + from_dict (monitor_daemon_state.py:288-307); agent_status_history.csv incremental at 1 Hz + O(window) filtering (AUDIT #157); presence every ~60 s. Fix keeping exact 250 ms freshness: (mtime, size)-gated loaders in SessionManager._load_state and MonitorDaemonState.load so a parse happens only when the writer changed the file -- daemon state would drop from ~6 parses/s to 0.5/s; sessions.json parses would drop to its write rate, which is itself N per tick until the ux-perf §4 incident is fixed.

incidents.ref: model_metadata.py:325 comment ('hot path calls lookup() constantly; re-stat only every few seconds')
incidents.title: Model catalog lookup on every render/tick
incidents.problem: lookup() is called per widget render and per daemon tick; naive implementation would stat/parse the catalog each time.
incidents.fix: 5 s TTL on re-stat (_ACTIVE_TTL_SECONDS, model_metadata.py:326-329) and a (path, mtime) parse cache holding a single vintage (333-360).
incidents.residual_risk: Verified bounded: <=2 stats per 5 s per process; parse only on mtime change.
