critic_gaps.label: tmux server as the shared single-threaded bottleneck: fleet-wide command budget, server-side cost, split-layout/grouped-session effects, and the stale-daemon capture amplifier
critic_gaps.why_missed: Every lane costed its own tmux subprocesses from the client side (fork/exec wall time per call) and two lanes (L1, L8) explicitly reported that tmux SERVER-side CPU per command was not isolated. No lane summed the fleet-wide command rate across TUI + daemon + hook handler + summarizer + web/sister pollers + follow-mode CLIs, and nobody read cli/split.py (the `overcode tmux` layout every user runs) or treated the tmux server (PID 24475 here: 151 CPU-min over 14.5 days, 0.9% now at 3 agents, 1 thread) as a third long-lived process whose single thread serialises every overcode command AND the human's keystrokes. The maintainer's 2026-09-20 notes (memory: tmux typing-lag investigation) already established that command COUNT, not capture depth, loads the server (~3 ms overhead per command; 20 agents at 4 Hz pushed display-message p90 from 4 ms to 15 ms) and that the nested client in the split layout round-trips the same server 2-3 times per keystroke - none of that reached the lanes.
critic_gaps.focus: Build ONE table of tmux commands/second at reference scale (N_AGENTS=50, R_HOOKS=5/s, S_SISTERS=5, dashboard open) by summing, with file:line for each: TUI fast path (tui.py:1397 via select_capture_sessions tui_logic.py:923: 1 focused capture at 4 Hz + N/4 per tick rotation = ~4+12.5/s at N=50), RealTmux 30 s cache refresh bursts (implementations.py:30-110, one list-* per property), launcher._list_tmux_windows_cheap every 10 s, _resize_agent_windows_async every 15 s (tui.py:821; tui_actions/view.py:83,114 display-message/resize-window), _sync_tmux_window/_fix_window_size_if_needed per navigation; daemon (monitor_daemon.py:1380 N captures per 2 s loop = 25/s; get_pane_pid per session at 1287 every 5 s and 1339 every 15 s = 13/s; list_windows at 380/972; send-keys heartbeats at 587 + exit_copy_mode_if_active); hook handler _detect_from_tmux_pane (hook_handler.py:263) once per hook event = 5/s; summarizer _capture_pane N per 5 s = 10/s (summarizer_component.py:129); web_api._capture_agent_pane (web_api.py:92) N per /api/status request x (dashboard 5 s + S_SISTERS x 10 s) = 10-60/s. Expect ~80-130 commands/s at reference and 300+ at stress; measure server-side cost per command TYPE on this machine by driving a synthetic loop against PID 24475 (ps -o %cpu / cumulative TIME delta) for capture-pane -e of 500 lines at 364x52 vs display-message vs list-windows, and measure display-message p50/p90 latency (the typing-lag proxy) at 20/50/100 commands/s. State the cliff as the command rate at which display-message p90 exceeds ~16 ms (one frame). Then examine the amplifier: tui_logic.select_capture_sessions captures every session NOT in daemon_known_ids every tick, and daemon_known_ids collapses when MonitorDaemonState.is_stale (monitor_daemon_state.py:308, interval + 30 s buffer) - combine L11's per-loop counters (84 sessions.json loads + 30 RMW per 15 sessions, 18.6 ms per load at 2000 entries) with the daemon's N captures to compute the (N_AGENTS, N_SESSIONS_TOTAL) point where tick wall time exceeds 32 s, at which the TUI falls back to N captures at 4 Hz (800/s at N=200) and the tmux server saturates, which slows the daemon further (positive feedback). Also read cli/split.py:196-237 and 915-935 (_setup_linked_session: grouped session doubles per-window client rendering; client-resized hook runs `resize-window -A` on EVERY window on every terminal resize = SIGWINCH to every agent, and the maintainer measured resize-window as not a no-op; window-size largest; history-limit 50000 on the linked session) and _setup_keybindings (268-330; verify all bindings are if-shell -F format-only so no shell spawns per key). Freshness requirement to state: focused pane preview 250 ms; other agents' status comes from the daemon at 2 s so their TUI captures only feed bash/subagent/auto-accept columns (can lag 5-10 s or be dropped in favour of daemon-published values); hook-handler capture must stay under Claude Code's hook timeout; keystroke echo through the tmux server must stay under one frame. Prefer fixes that cut command count at equal freshness: daemon publishing the pane-derived columns so the TUI never captures non-focused panes; one `capture-pane` result shared between detector, summarizer and web_api per loop; batching via a single tmux control-mode client or `tmux -C` instead of one process per command; and removing the stale->full-capture fallback (fall back to daemon-published status with a staleness banner, not to N x 4 Hz captures).

critic_gaps.label: No visibility/presence gating: the entire TUI workload (4 Hz capture, 1 Hz burn-rate transcript parse, 5 s stats sweep, 30 s timeline, full render pipeline) runs unchanged when no tmux client is attached, the TUI window is not active, or the screen is locked/user idle - the shape of the '110% CPU for 15 hours' report
critic_gaps.why_missed: Lanes were organised by timer/site and asked 'what does this cost per tick'; none asked 'is anyone looking'. grep shows the only idle gate in the TUI is the summarizer's keypress-idle auto-pause (tui.py:1929-1947, _last_keypress set in on_key tui.py:4090) - the fast path (601), stats (604), daemon status (605), timeline (607), sisters (612/615), jobs (617/619) and resize (623) timers have no attach/visibility/presence condition, and the render pipeline (Textual) draws frames regardless of whether a tmux client is attached to the TUI's pane. Meanwhile the daemon already computes presence (Quartz CGEventSourceSecondsSinceLastEventType idle seconds + screen-lock, presence_logger.py:109-125, logged every sample interval to presence_log.csv with a tui_active flag from the TUI heartbeat, presence_logger.py:231-258), and tmux exposes #{session_attached}/#{window_active}/#{client_activity} cheaply - nobody connected the two. The `q`-quit plan in the maintainer's memory (make q stop the viewer to free CPU) confirms the unattended-TUI cost is the real complaint, but that plan only covers explicit quit, not detached/locked/idle sessions, and this machine's TUI (PID 71557) has burned 24.6% of a core for 19 h including overnight.
critic_gaps.focus: Enumerate, per TUI timer (tui.py:583-623) and per widget refresh (tui_log_panel.py:60, daemon_panel.py:40, Header clock), which of its outputs are consumed by anything OTHER than the human looking at the screen: (a) MacNotifier stall bells (tui.py:1860-1871 via compute_stall_state) - needed while the user is in another app but NOT while the screen is locked/idle, and derivable from daemon-published statuses (monitor_daemon_state) at 2 s without any TUI capture; (b) write_tui_heartbeat/signal_activity (settings.py:523,718) that the daemon's presence logger and _interruptible_sleep read - keypress-driven, unaffected; (c) sister/web consumers - served by the daemon and web server, not the TUI; (d) _save_prefs, status_changes.csv, event_loop_timing.csv - diagnostics. Conclude that when the TUI is invisible its required freshness for every rendered value is zero and only (a) survives. Then define the visibility signal and its cost: tmux `display-message -p '#{session_attached} #{window_active} #{client_activity}'` for the TUI's own pane (one command, can piggyback on the existing 10 s _list_tmux_windows_cheap call in launcher.py:931 or on tmux focus-events which cli/split.py:746 already turns on globally, delivering focus-in/out escape sequences Textual surfaces as AppFocus/AppBlur events - check whether tui.py handles on_app_focus/on_app_blur at all), plus the daemon's presence state (idle seconds/locked) read from monitor_daemon_state or the last presence_log.csv row (already parsed by StatusTimeline.fetch_history_data). Specify a 'parked' mode that keeps the daemon untouched, stops pane captures, transcript parsing, git scans, timeline/presence CSV reads and Textual refresh calls entirely while invisible, and resumes at full cadence on the first focus-in/keypress/attach with an immediate forced tick (so perceived freshness on return is one tick, not one interval). Quantify the saving from L0's decomposition (burn-rate parse 13.4%, main-thread render 2.7%, fast path 2-3%, presence CSV 0.7%, stats 0.4% of a core at N=3; scale to the N=50/200 numbers the other lanes produced) and state the residual cost the daemon still carries alone. Also check the split layout's _hold_wrapper (cli/split.py:483-508) and the q-quit plan interplay so a parked TUI and a quit TUI behave consistently, and confirm the TUI still writes its heartbeat while parked so the daemon's tui_active presence flag does not flip and change daemon behaviour (presence_logger.py:231, monitor_daemon.py:183).

critic_gaps.label: Timer phase alignment: the 5/10/15/30 s timers all fire in the same instant, producing a thread + tmux-fork + main-thread-callback burst every 5 s; the TUI's own 10 Hz event-loop probe (never analysed by any lane) shows main-thread stalls >150 ms are 7x more frequent in that 1-second window and the sister apply callback measures p99 179 ms / max 469 ms on the main thread although it only kicks a worker
critic_gaps.why_missed: Lanes costed each timer in isolation and L14 estimated main-thread occupancy per callback, but nobody looked at the scheduling: tui.py:599-623 creates refresh_sessions (10 s), update_focused_status (0.25 s), _update_stats_async (5 s), update_timeline (30 s), _poll_sisters (10 s), _refresh_jobs (5 s) and _periodic_agent_resize (15 s) in the same on_mount instant with no phase offset (only update_daemon_status 1.7 s, summaries 3.3 s, heartbeat flush 4.5 s and status-change flush 5.0 s are staggered), so every 5 s boundary starts 2-6 thread workers and their subprocess fan-outs at once and their call_from_thread apply callbacks then queue back-to-back on the render thread, contending for the GIL with the 1 Hz burn-rate JSON parse. Ground truth existed on disk the whole time: ~/.overcode/sessions/agents/diagnostics/event_loop_timing.csv (45 MB, 1.17 M rows of 100 ms heartbeats plus apply_* markers, written by tui.py:4237-4275) - L0 listed the file's size but no lane read it. My read-only analysis of the last 1.04 M rows (14 h): heartbeat delta p50 37 ms, p99 104 ms, p99.9 160 ms, max 659 ms; gaps >150 ms per 1-s phase bucket of the 10-s grid anchored on apply_stats_start: 340 in the bucket at the 5-s timer boundary vs 27-100 in every other bucket (0.69% vs ~0.09%), and 440 of them in the two 0.5-s buckets 4.0-5.0 s of the 5-s grid vs ~40 elsewhere; main-thread time inside callbacks: apply_status 4 Hz p50 1.1 / p99 4.6 / max 200 ms, apply_daemon p99 1.2 ms, apply_stats p99 4.1 / max 71 ms, apply_sisters p90 28 / p99 179 / max 469 ms with 53 of the >200 ms gaps immediately preceded by apply_sisters_end - yet _apply_remote_sessions (tui.py:1645-1655) only assigns a list and calls refresh_sessions() which merely starts the _fetch_sessions_async worker (886-898), so its 28-469 ms is inflation from the co-firing 10-s burst (GIL hand-off to launcher.list_sessions/poll_all/stats threads, worker cancel/create in WorkerManager) rather than its own work.
